[[New Japan Pro-Wrestling|NJPW]] Dojo{{cite web|url=http://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=1072&name=Ultimo+Dragon|title=Ultimo Dragon|publisher=cagematch.net|access-date=2016-10-17}} |debut = May 13, 1987 |retired = }} {{nihongo|'''Yoshihiro Asai'''|浅井嘉浩|Asai Yoshihiro|born December 12, 1966}}, better known by his [[ring name]] {{nihongo|'''Último Dragón'''|ウルティモ・ドラゴン|Urutimo Doragon}},{{cite web|url=http://www.onlineworldofwrestling.com/profiles/u/ultimo-dragon.html|title=Ultimo Dragon|publisher=Online World of Wrestling|access-date=2009-08-14}} is a Japanese [[Professional wrestling|professional wrestler]] signed to [[Dragon Gate (wrestling)|Dragon Gate]], where he acts as an in-ring talent, trainer and senior advisor. In addition to having trained in Japan, Asai learned to wrestle in the ''[[lucha libre]]'' style while working in [[Mexico]]. He is credited with popularizing the "[[Moonsault#Springboard moonsault|Asai Moonsault]]". On October 11, 1996, Asai won the [[J-Crown]], a unification of eight lower weight division titles from various international promotions. At the time, he already held the [[NWA World Middleweight Championship]] and during this reign he also became the [[WWE Cruiserweight Championship (1991–2007)|WCW Cruiserweight Champion]]. From December 29, 1996, through January 4, 1997, he concurrently held ten titles,{{cite web|last=Molinaro|first=John|title=A Quiet End for Ultimo Dragon|work=SLAM! Wrestling|publisher=[[Canadian Online Explorer]]|date=October 28, 1999|url=http://www.canoe.com/SlamWrestlingEditorial/oct28_molinaro.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000901042630/http://www.canoe.com/SlamWrestlingEditorial/oct28_molinaro.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 1, 2000|access-date=2008-03-15}} making him the most simultaneously-decorated wrestler in history until [[Mercedes Moné]] broke his record in 2025. From 2013 until 2019, he competed primarily for [[All Japan Pro Wrestling]] (AJPW) as a freelancer. In 2019, he joined Dragon Gate as a senior advisor and wrestler. ==Professional wrestling career== ===Early years (1984–1996)=== [[File:究極龍.jpg|thumb|left|Asai performing as Último Dragón]] Asai trained in the [[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]] (NJPW) [[NJPW Dojo|dojo]] in 1987, but was not drafted up by the promotion due to his small size. He moved to Mexico where he joined the [[Universal Wrestling Association]] and subsequently won the [[UWA World Welterweight Championship]] in 1988. In March 1990, he joined the [[Universal Wrestling Federation (Japan)|Universal Wrestling Federation]] in Japan. He also competed in the [[Universal Lucha Libre]] promotion founded by his mentor [[Gran Hamada]]. In 1991, he signed with the Mexican [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL) promotion. In CMLL, he adopted the Último Dragón mask and persona. "Último Dragón", which means "Last Dragon" in Spanish, was initially a [[List of professional wrestling terms#Gimmick|gimmick]] that saw Asai claiming to be the last student taught by legendary martial artist [[Bruce Lee]], whose nickname was "The Dragon". The gimmick was later dropped, but the name remained. When he returned to Japan in 1992, he chose to join [[Super World of Sports]]. Late in 1992, [[Último Dragoncito|Misteriosito]] was turned into "Último Dragoncito", a [[Mini-Estrella]] version of Asai. After SWS closed, Asai signed with the Japanese [[WAR (wrestling promotion)|WAR]] promotion, and due to co-promoting, he was able to wrestle for NJPW. In Japan, he became IWGP Junior heavyweight champion twice, and in Mexico, he held various titles. In later years, he wrestled for [[Lucha Libre AAA World Wide|AAA]].{{cite news|author=Chatra, Mo|title=Enter the Dragon|pages=24–25|work=Power Slam Magazine|id=109|date=August 2003|publisher=SW Publishing LTD|location=[[Lancaster, Lancashire]], England}} ===World Championship Wrestling (1996–1998)=== [[File:Ultimo Dragon & Sonny Onoo (41196207164).jpg|thumb|right|175px|Último Dragón and former manager [[Sonny Onoo]] in 2017]] Asai made his American debut for the [[World Championship Wrestling]] (WCW) promotion in August 1996 initially under the mistranslated name "Ultimate Dragon". He was referred to by this name for over a year in WCW until they reverted to using his Spanish ring name.{{cite web|url=http://bodyslamming.com/other/ultimo.html |title=Japanese Superstars - Ultimo Dragon |access-date=March 1, 2008 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071208040310/http://bodyslamming.com/other/ultimo.html |archive-date=December 8, 2007 }} He quickly was pushed into the lime-light of the WCW Cruiserweight division with [[Sonny Onoo]] as his manager. He was instantly a heel based upon the fact he was Japanese and Onoo was his manager. He made his WCW pay-per view debut in 1996's [[WCW Hog Wild|Hog Wild]] against [[Rey Mysterio|Rey Misterio Jr.]] for the [[WCW Cruiserweight Championship]] but lost. He got back the win at [[WCW World War 3 (1996)]] when he returned to WCW as the [[J-Crown]] champion. Between November 24, 1996 and January 4, 1997 Último Dragón held the WWF Light Heavyweight title simultaneously with the WCW Cruiserweight title. He then feuded with [[Dean Malenko]] for the WCW Cruiserweight title which he won at Starrcade 1996. Dragon later dropped the WCW Cruiserweight title back to Malenko but his stock was rising as he won the [[WCW World Television Championship]] from [[Prince Iaukea]] but lost it to [[William Regal|Steven Regal]]. He then turned on Onoo and began a face run and (kayfabe) moved back to Mexico and regained the World Television title from Regal before losing to [[Alex Wright]] at [[Clash of the Champions#Clash of the Champions XXXV|Clash of the Champions XXXV]]. He would then win the WCW Cruiserweight title one last time from [[Eddie Guerrero]], before losing the title on the first ''[[WCW Thunder]]'' to [[Juventud Guerrera]]. He then suffered an arm injury in 1998 that required surgery. The operation was botched, causing [[Seddon's classification|nerve damage]]. It was thought that this would force an end of his career and he announced his retirement in November. ===Toryumon (1997–2003)=== In 1997, Asai then became a trainer and founded the [[Toryumon (Último Dragón)|Último Dragón Gym]], where he trained three classes of students, "Toryumon Japan", "Toryumon 2000 Project" (T2P), and "Toryumon X". His first class of students, which included [[Don Fujii|Don Fuji]], [[Dragon Kid]], [[Magnum Tokyo]], [[Nobuhiko Oshima|Cima]] and [[Takahiro Suwa|Suwa]], worked for WCW early in their career.{{cite news | author = Chatra, Mo | title = Toryumon Uncovered| pages= 34–35 | work = Power Slam Magazine | id = 116 | date = March 2005 | publisher=SW Publishing LTD | location=[[Lancaster, Lancashire]], England}} In 1998, Asai began co-promoting [[IWRG|Grupo Internacional Revolución]] (IWRG) based out of Mexico, where he trained several of the top young wrestlers.{{cite web|url=http://slam.canoe.com/SlamWrestlingChats/apr26_molinaro.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309144634/http://slam.canoe.com/SlamWrestlingChats/apr26_molinaro.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 9, 2016|title=SLAM! Wrestling – John Molinaro Chat|website=canoe.com}} In 1999, a promotion named [[Toryumon (Último Dragón)|Toryumon]] opened, with the vast majority of the roster having been trained by Asai. Toryumon was later renamed [[Dragon Gate (wrestling)|Dragon Gate]] as Asai parted ways with the promotion. He continued to train students at his gym. In 2002, Asai underwent another surgery to repair the damage done to his arm in hopes of returning to wrestling. In late 2002 Ultimo Dragon was in talks with [[WWE|World Wrestling Entertainment]] for another shot at a United States run. To get back into ring shape he returned to action for his T2P and Toryumon Mexico promotions. On November 26, he teamed with former WCW wrestlers [[Norman Smiley]] and [[Perry Saturn]] in a win against [[Masaaki Mochizuki]], [[Kenichiro Arai]] and [[Toru Owashi]] for T2P. On December 7 he teamed with Mochizuki and [[Dragon Kid]] in a win over the team of [[Bestia Salvaje]], [[Scorpio Jr.]] and El Duende for Toryumon Mexico. ===World Wrestling Entertainment (2003–2004)=== In the spring of 2003, he signed with [[WWE|World Wrestling Entertainment]] as the ''Último Dragón'', seeking to realize his two lifelong goals of competing in [[Madison Square Garden]] and performing at [[WrestleMania]]. He was brought in on the heels of the signing of [[Rey Mysterio]] on the belief that he would make as big of an impact as Mysterio did upon his WWE debut. Asai made his WWE debut in dark match victories against [[Rico Constantino|Rico]], [[Crash Holly]] and [[Shannon Moore]] as they debuted a series of video packages hyping the debut of Dragon on ''[[WWE SmackDown|SmackDown!]]''. He made his WWE television debut at Madison Square Garden on June 26, 2003 episode of ''SmackDown!'' in a match with Shannon Moore, where he debuted his finisher, the Asai DDT (a standing shiranui), to the American wrestling audience. Throughout the summer he competed in a tournament for the [[WWE United States Championship]] beating [[Jamie Noble]] but losing to eventual winner, [[Eddie Guerrero]]. He quickly rebounded by beating Kanyon in a ''[[WWE Heat]]'' match taped before [[Vengeance (2003)|Vengeance]]. He then wrestled on ''[[WWE Velocity]]'' for the next few weeks, leading to a match with Rey Mysterio on ''SmackDown''. Dragon won the match only after [[Yoshihiro Tajiri|Tajiri]] interfered and showed respect to Dragon due to their Japanese heritage. The next week Dragon teamed with Mysterio to take on Tajiri and [[Nunzio (wrestler)|Nunzio]]. After this match, he was not seen on ''SmackDown!'' for several months until the build for the Cruiserweight Open at [[WrestleMania XX]]. At the event, Dragon participated in the Open. Dragon's WrestleMania resulted in one of WrestleMania's most famous blunders, tripping as he entered the arena from the backstage area and tripping as he was going up the turnbuckle for a pose.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lJqmVhl7Rmc |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/lJqmVhl7Rmc| archive-date=2021-12-12 |url-status=live|title=Ultimo Dragon slips at Wrestlemania falls trips classic |website=[[YouTube]]|date=May 12, 2008 |access-date=May 19, 2014}}{{cbignore}} The first trip was edited out of the WrestleMania XX DVD, but the second wasn't.{{cite web |url=http://www.wrestlingdvdnews.com/review-wrestlemania-xx-20-dvd/3699/ |title=Review: WWE Wrestlemania XX (20) DVD |work=WrestlingDVDNews.com |author=Brett Mix |date=August 11, 2010 |access-date=May 19, 2014}} After the open, he faced [[Chavo Guerrero Jr.|Chavo Guerrero]] and Nunzio in his last WWE matches. On April 22, 2004, WWE announced that Asai asked for his release from WWE when he knew WWE wanted to unmask him and went back to Japan immediately.{{cite web | url=https://solowrestling.mundodeportivo.com/new/114298-ultimo-dragon-asegura-que-en-wwe-querian-desenmascararlo | title=Último Dragón asegura que en WWE querían desenmascararlo | date=November 16, 2022 }} ===Return to Japan (2004–present)=== One month after being released from WWE, Asai quickly picked up a New Japan tour on May 1, 2004. He returned to Mexico by occasionally wrestling for [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL). He also took part in the short lived Japanese independent promotion Dragondoor, ran by one of his students Noriaki Kawabata using mostly T2P and Toryumon X graduates. He would wrestle in matches against [[Último Guerrero]] and various other stars who wrestled in Mexico or Japanese based lucha libre promotions. Since the fall of Dragondoor he went back to Mexico to run another class of the Toryumon school, which has led to some standouts in [[Hajime Ohara]], [[Kazuchika Okada]] and Pequeño Ninja. The rest of the Toryumon students along with Asai joined the [[Tatsumi Fujinami]] promoted Dradition promotion in Japan. In 2006, Asai began promoting the annual "Toryumon Mexico: Dragon Mania" wrestling show.{{cite web | url=http://www.accelerator3359.com/Wrestling/bios/ultimo.html | title=Ultimo Guerrero Profile |publisher=Wrestling Accelerator}} He also wrestled at UWA Hardcore Wrestling based outside of Toronto, Ontario, Canada. He has wrestled against [[Sonjay Dutt]], [[Matt Cross (wrestler)|M-Dogg 20]], [[Chris Sabin]], [[Alex Shelley]], [[Jyushin Thunder Liger]] and [[Rocky Romero|Black Tiger]] all in the UWA. Since then he has been working in Japan for various independent promotions such as Pro Wrestling Kageki and [[Michinoku Pro]]. He has also been to Mexico as well as in Spain, working for Nu Wrestling Evolution. On December 15, 2013, Dragón defeated [[Yoshinobu Kanemaru]] to win [[All Japan Pro Wrestling]]'s [[World Junior Heavyweight Championship (AJPW)|World Junior Heavyweight Championship]].{{cite web | url = http://battle-news.com/battle/2013/12/002058.php | title = 激動だった全日本の1年を斧爆弾で締めくくった大森が、新年一発目の三冠挑戦を表明！究極龍が悲願の世界Jr王座奪取！ | date=December 16, 2013 | access-date=2013-12-15 | work=Battle News | language=ja}} He lost the title to [[Atsushi Aoki]] on May 29, 2014.{{cite web|url=http://www.all-japan.co.jp/post_tour/8112/ |title=2014 スーパーパワーシリーズ 東京･後楽園ホール【最終戦】 |access-date=2014-05-29 |work=[[All Japan Pro Wrestling]] |language=ja |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140529203404/http://www.all-japan.co.jp/post_tour/8112/ |archive-date=May 29, 2014 }} On August 27, 2017, he regained the title by defeating [[Yoshihiro Tajiri|Tajiri]]. On March 22, 2015, Dragón won another title in All Japan, when he and Kanemaru defeated [[Mitsuya Nagai]] and [[Takeshi Minamino]] for the [[All Asia Tag Team Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.all-japan.co.jp/archives/match/【3-22】-2015-ドリームパワーシリーズ%E3%80%80福岡大会/|script-title=ja:【3.22】 2015 ドリームパワーシリーズ 福岡大会|date=March 22, 2015|access-date=2015-03-22|work=[[All Japan Pro Wrestling]]|language=ja|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150409125344/https://www.all-japan.co.jp/archives/match/%E3%80%903-22%E3%80%91-2015-%E3%83%89%E3%83%AA%E3%83%BC%E3%83%A0%E3%83%91%E3%83%AF%E3%83%BC%E3%82%B7%E3%83%AA%E3%83%BC%E3%82%BA%E3%80%80%E7%A6%8F%E5%B2%A1%E5%A4%A7%E4%BC%9A/|archive-date=April 9, 2015|df=mdy-all}} They vacated the title on October 14.{{cite web|url=https://www.all-japan.co.jp/archives/news/金丸義信選手＆ウルティモ・ドラゴン選手アジア/|script-title=ja:金丸義信選手＆ウルティモ・ドラゴン選手アジアタッグ返上のお知らせ|date=October 14, 2015|access-date=2015-10-14|work=[[All Japan Pro Wrestling]]|language=ja}}{{Dead link|date=January 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On August 30 and 31, 2014, Dragón participated in a show in [[Pyongyang]], [[North Korea]] promoted by the [[Inoki Genome Federation]]. He defeated [[Hajime Ohara]] on the first day and Heddi French on the second in singles matches.{{cite web | url = http://www.igf.jp/event/pyongyang/ | title = インターナショナル・プロレスリング・フェスティバルin平壌 | access-date = 2015-03-22 | work = [[Inoki Genome Federation]] | language = ja | archive-date = September 5, 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140905020247/http://www.igf.jp/event/pyongyang/ | url-status = dead }} ==Acting career== Ultimo Dragon starred in two films in 2008. The first was ''[[Bloodstained Memoirs]]'', also starring [[Chris Jericho]], [[Rob Van Dam]], [[Mick Foley]] and [[Keiji Muto]]. Unnamed daughter }} {{nihongo|'''Edward Elric'''|エドワード・エルリック|Edowādo Erurikku|lead=yes}} is a fictional character and the titular protagonist of the ''[[Fullmetal Alchemist]]'' [[manga]] series created by [[Hiromu Arakawa]]. Edward, titled the {{nihongo|'''Fullmetal Alchemist'''|鋼の錬金術師|Hagane no Renkinjutsushi|{{lit.|Alchemist of Steel}}}}, is the youngest State Alchemist in the history of the [[fictional country]] of Amestris. His left leg was divinely severed in a failed attempt to resurrect his dead mother, and then his right arm was taken in exchange for his brother's soul. His missing limbs have been replaced with [[Retrofuturism|sophisticated]] [[Prosthesis|prosthetics]] called {{nihongo|automail|{{ruby|機械鎧|オートメイル}}|ōtomeiru}}. He and his younger brother, [[Alphonse Elric|Alphonse]], who lost his entire body and is spiritually bound to a suit of armor, scour the world in search of the [[Philosopher's stone|Philosopher's Stone]] in the hopes of restoring their bodies. Edward has appeared in other media from the series, including [[video game]]s, [[original video animation]]s (OVAs) and [[light novel]]s. Numerous publications in various media have been written on the subject of Edward's character. Reviewers praised Edward as a balance between the typical clever kid and the stubborn kid persona. Additionally, his comedic moments have been celebrated as some of the best moments in the series. His Japanese and English voice actors, [[Romi Park]] and [[Vic Mignogna]], have both been praised for their performances as Edward and have won several awards for their work. Numerous pieces of merchandise have been released bearing Edward's likeness, including key chains and action figures. ==Creation and conception== Author [[Hiromu Arakawa]] integrated several social problems into the plot, such as the way Edward and Alphonse live as brothers after the death of their mother, Trisha. She also looks at how the brothers help people all over the country to gain an understanding of the meaning of family.{{Cite journal |title=Equivalent Change |journal=[[Newtype USA]] |volume=5 |issue=1 |page=24 | date=January 2006 }} When describing the character's personality, Arakawa comments that after his father's departure from home and his mother's death, Edward tried to replace the role of the man for the Elric family. As a result, Van Hohenheim's reappearance caused a shocking and terrified reaction in the character.{{cite book | last=Arakawa | first=Hiromu | title=Fullmetal Alchemist Rough Sketch Gallery| year=2006 | publisher=Square Enix|page=29| isbn=978-4-7575-1695-3 }} Arakawa has noted that Edward is one of her favorite characters from the series, although she denied having the same personality as him when one of her assistants mentioned it.{{cite book|author=Arakawa, Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist Profiles|pages=100–105|year=2006|publisher=Viz Media|isbn=978-1-4215-0768-2 }} When comparing the two brothers during the time Alphonse obtained the ability to use alchemy without a circle like Edward, Arakawa stated nobody was better at alchemy as the two had different preferences in the same way as other alchemist appearing in the series.{{cite book | last=Arakawa | first=Hiromu | title=鋼の錬金術師 パーフェクトガイドブック 2| year=2005 | publisher=Square Enix|pages=168–172| isbn=978-4-7575-1426-3 }} Although she claims she has not thought of the characters' birthdates, Arakawa noted that she decided Edward's birthdate during the series' serialization. During a chapter in which it was mentioned that Edward was about to be 16, winter was about to begin in Hokkaido, Arakawa's birthplace, so it was decided Edward's birthdate would be in winter.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 12|year=2007|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|page=184|isbn=978-1-4215-0839-9}} In a common [[slapstick]] gag from the series, Edward is often struck by Winry Rockbell's [[wrench]]. While commenting that Edward has the ability to easily dodge her, Arakawa comments that he gets hit on purpose as a result of his personality.{{cite book | last=Arakawa | first=Hiromu | title=荒川弘イラスト集 FULLMETAL ALCHEMIST 3 | year=2011 | publisher=Square Enix|page=134| isbn=978-4-7575-3220-5}} The director of the first anime series, [[Seiji Mizushima]], says that in the development of the story Edward "evolves and devolves"; Mizushima comments that Edward is continuously overcoming inner struggles in order to determine how to grow up. The appearance of his automail in the anime is used to symbolize the intangibles of his character, making viewers note that Edward lost something important.{{Cite journal |title=Fullmetal Alchemist |journal=[[Newtype USA]] |volume=5 |issue=3 |page=32 | date=March 2006 }} In a prototype from the series, Edward was an eighteen-year-old teenager travelling alongside his father whose soul sealed in a [[flying squirrel]]. Edward's prototype had an average height, but retained his automail. In order to fit with the readers from the manga magazine ''Monthly Shonen Gangan'', Edward's traits were further modified, leaving his current one. His height was reduced in order to contrast with Alphonse's huge armor.{{cite journal | last=Arakawa | first=Hiromu | journal=TV Bros|title=アニメ開始ごろ|date=December 2003 |url=http://www3.atwiki.jp/fa/pages/38.html }} In the design of the character, Arakawa is often worried about not making his automail too bulky to avoid balancing it by increasing Edward's muscles, making his appearance unsuitable for his age.{{cite book | last=Arakawa | first=Hiromu | title=Fullmetal Alchemist Rough Sketch Gallery| year=2006 | publisher=Square Enix|page=7| isbn=978-4-7575-1695-3 }} She has also often drawn the character in full body length, but at one point noticed she made it too tall.{{cite book | last=Arakawa | first=Hiromu | title=Fullmetal Alchemist Rough Sketch Gallery| year=2006 | publisher=Square Enix|page=15| isbn=978-4-7575-1695-3 }}{{cite book | last=Arakawa | first=Hiromu | title=Fullmetal Alchemist Rough Sketch Gallery| year=2006 | publisher=Square Enix|page=23| isbn=978-4-7575-1695-3 }} As the manga continued serialization, Arakawa found that she drew Edward half naked several times even more than [[List of Fullmetal Alchemist characters#Alex Louis Armstrong|Alex Louis Armstrong]] who tends to show his torso. While stating that this was because she wanted to draw Edward's automail, she commented that it was common for men to walk in underwear at their homes.{{cite book | last=Arakawa | first=Hiromu | title=The Art Of Fullmetal Alchemist| year=2005 | publisher=Viz Media|pages=94–95| isbn=978-1-4215-0158-1 }} ===Casting=== {{multiple image | align = right | total_width = 400 | image1 = Romi Park on Terry Tsuchiya's Car Talk, June 27, 2025 10m 11s.png | alt1 = A photo of Romi Park | image2 = Vic Mignogna by Gage Skidmore 2.jpg | alt2 = A photo of Vic Mignogna | image3 = Yamada Ryosuke (cropped).jpg| | alt3 = A photo of Ryosuke Yamada | footer = [[Romi Park]] (left) and [[Vic Mignogna]] (middle) voice Edward in Japanese and English, respectively. [[Ryosuke Yamada]] (right) portrayed him in the live-action films. }} In the Japanese version of ''Fullmetal Alchemist''{{'}}s anime adaptations, Edward has been voiced by [[Romi Park]]. In the English version, the role has been played by [[Vic Mignogna]].{{cite episode|title=Those Who Challenge the Sun|airdate=November 6, 2004|credits=Director: Seiji Mizushima|series=Fullmetal Alchemist|network=Cartoon Network}} Mignogna has stated that performing Edward may be his biggest [[voice acting]] achievement since fans do not compare him with Park, noting that their voices are not similar and that he did not plan to sound like her.{{cite web|title=Interview with Vic Mignogna|url=http://www.mania.com/being-brief-discussion-vic-mignogna_article_84273.html|author=Jeng, Way|date=April 19, 2005|publisher=Mania Entertainment|access-date=April 2, 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081207030519/http://www.mania.com/being-brief-discussion-vic-mignogna_article_84273.html|archive-date=December 7, 2008}} Additionally, in [[Fullmetal Alchemist (film)|the 2017 live-action film]] based on the series, Edward is portrayed by [[Ryosuke Yamada]].{{cite web|url=http://www.crunchyroll.com/anime-news/2016/04/03-1/dean-fujioka-and-others-join-live-action-fullmetal-alchemist-film|title=Dean Fujioka and Others Join Live-Action "Fullmetal Alchemist" Film|publisher=Crunchyroll|access-date=April 3, 2016|date=April 3, 2016|archive-date=April 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160406024335/http://www.crunchyroll.com/anime-news/2016/04/03-1/dean-fujioka-and-others-join-live-action-fullmetal-alchemist-film|url-status=dead}} Yamada thinks his short stature might be work as an advantage due to one of Edward's most common characteristics is his low height. Studying Arakawa's manga, Yamada tried imitating Edward's other signature actions such the way he runs. A fan of the series, the actor expressed happiness with the role he was given. Nevertheless, he asked at [[Anime Expo]] 2017 if anything from him looked "weird" which resulted in praise from the audience. During questions, Yamada said that one of the most difficult scenes about his acting is interacting with Alphonse as a result of the latter being CGI. As a result, in the shooting of some scenes the staff had a person in Alphonse's place so that Yamada had a better way to act.{{cite web|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/convention/2017/anime-expo/fullmetal-alchemist-live-action-film-panel-q-a/.118435|title=Fullmetal Alchemist Live-Action Film Panel + Q&A|last=Loveridge|first=Lynzee|website=[[Anime News Network]]|access-date=July 5, 2017|date=July 5, 2017|archive-date=August 29, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829215515/https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/convention/2017/anime-expo/fullmetal-alchemist-live-action-film-panel-q-a/.118435|url-status=live}} ==Appearances== ===In ''Fullmetal Alchemist''=== Edward was born in a small town named Resembool in the nation of Amestris, living with his younger brother [[Alphonse Elric|Alphonse]] and their parents [[List of Fullmetal Alchemist characters#Trisha Elric|Trisha Elric]] and [[Van Hohenheim]]. After Hohenheim left the family on a journey early in their lives, Edward developed a loathing for their father as he and Alphonse learned to use [[alchemy]] before Trisha died of an illness years later. The two brothers concentrated on studying alchemy in the hopes of bringing their mother back to life, and trained with a skilled alchemist named [[List of Fullmetal Alchemist characters#Izumi Curtis|Izumi Curtis]].{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 5|year=2006|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 21|isbn=978-1-4215-0175-8}} When they make the attempt to revive their mother, it failed and the brothers paid a bigger price via the Law of Equivalent Exchange: which states that every outcome requires an equal payment.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 1|year=2005|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 4|isbn=978-1-59116-920-8}} Edward lost his left leg while meeting the metaphysical being known as {{nihongo4|Truth|真理|Shinri}}, gaining great knowledge as well as the prodigious ability to perform transmutations just by clapping his hands together without the need of a Transmutation Circle.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 2|year=2005|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 6|page=94|isbn=978-1-59116-923-9}} As Alphonse's entire being was taken by Truth, Edward uses his newly gained knowledge in sacrificing his own right arm to retrieve Alphonse's soul and bind it to a nearby suit of armor. While being outfitted prosthetic "automail" limbs by the grandmother of his childhood friend, [[Winry Rockbell]], Edward became motivated to restore Alphonse,{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 4|year=2005|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 15|page=98|isbn=978-1-59116-929-1}} Edward joins the State Military due to Roy Mustang's guide. He becomes the youngest State Alchemist, receiving the title of "Fullmetal Alchemist" shortly thereafter from the military head, [[List of Fullmetal Alchemist characters#King Bradley|Führer King Bradley]]. For the next few years, the Elric Brothers begin an extensive search for the legendary Philosopher's Stone in order to restore their bodies.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 1|year=2005|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 2|page=82|isbn=978-1-59116-920-8}} Besides his abilities as an alchemist, Edward is a formidable fighter as a result of his training with Izumi, who had extensively trained both brothers in [[martial arts]].{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 6|year=2006|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 23|isbn=978-1-4215-0319-6|pages=61–63}} During their search for the Stone, Edward and Alphonse had a near-death experience when attacked by [[Scar (Fullmetal Alchemist)|Scar]], a vengeful Ishvalan targeting State Alchemists for the mass murder of his people during the Ishvalan Civil War. They also meet a former State Alchemist Tim Marcoh who gives them the method of creating a Philosopher's Stone. The brothers later get revelations in the form of immortal beings known as the [[List of Fullmetal Alchemist characters#Homunculi|homunculi]].{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 6|year=2006|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 24|isbn=978-1-4215-0319-6}} When Edward and Alphonse discover that the homunculi and the Philosopher's Stone are related, they work together with Mustang and the Xingese prince Lin Yao to find them.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 11|year=2007|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 45|isbn=978-1-4215-0838-2}} But the Elric brothers meet the homunculus whom the homunculi call "[[Father (Fullmetal Alchemist)|Father]]," who is the true leader of Amestris with Bradley being a human-based homunculus. The brothers are forced to keep working with the military as Bradley uses Winry as a hostage.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 14|year=2007|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 57|isbn=978-1-4215-1379-9}} Forced to comply, the Elrics travel to the northern area of the country in order where they eventually reveal what they know to General [[List of Fullmetal Alchemist characters#Olivier Mira Armstrong|Olivier Mira Armstrong]] while dealing with the homunculus Sloth.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 17|year=2008|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 67|isbn=978-1-4215-2161-9}} Shortly after their arrival, the State Alchemist [[List of Fullmetal Alchemist characters#Solf J. Kimblee|Solf J. Kimblee]] bring Winry to the north as a hostage, unbeknownst to Winry, to force Edward's help in hunting Scar.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 17|year=2008|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 69|isbn=978-1-4215-2161-9}} But the brothers and Scar made their peace as they end up using his help so Alphonse can take Winry to safety.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 18|year=2009|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 73|isbn=978-1-4215-2536-5}} Upon their success, joined by Lin after he willingly became a host for Greed, Edward learns the Father's full plan of making a massive human transmutation circle out of the country of Amestris to create a Philosopher's Stone. Edward later reunites with Alphonse and their father as they and their allies formulate an attack on Central City from all sides.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 20|year=2009|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 83|isbn=978-1-4215-3034-5}} The group make their way into the underground complex while dispatching many of the homunculi, but the Elric Brothers, Izumi, Honenhiem, and Mustang are captured by Father who uses them to absorb the souls of Amestrians to absorb the being beyond the Gate of Truth.{{cite book|author=Arakawa, Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 25|chapter=Chapter 102|year=2011|publisher=Viz Media|isbn=978-1-4215-3924-9}} But Honenheim and Scar act out their backup plans to return the recently stolen souls to their bodies and enable every alchemist to fighting the severely weakened Father. Joining the fray after defeating Pride, Edward loses his automail while battling Father. Alphonse transmutes his soul in order to restore Edward's original flesh-and-blood arm.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 27|url=https://archive.org/details/fullmetalalchemi0001arak|url-access=registration|year=2011|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 107|isbn=978-1-4215-3984-3}} After defeating Father, Edward manages to bring Alphonse back by sacrificing his own ability to use alchemy. The brothers return to their hometown to live normal lives, but are motivated by the memories of Nina and others they failed to save to learn new methods of alchemy to prevent such tragedies from being repeated. Two years later, Edward decides to head westward for their research with Winry accompanying him as they progressively developed a romantic relationship over the course of their adventure and eventually confessed their feelings to each other.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 15|year=2007|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 58|isbn=978-1-4215-1380-5}} In the epilogue, Edward and Winry are revealed to have married and have a son and daughter together.{{cite book|last=Arakawa|first=Hiromu|title=Fullmetal Alchemist, Volume 27|url=https://archive.org/details/fullmetalalchemi0001arak|url-access=registration|year=2011|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|chapter=Chapter 108|isbn=978-1-4215-3984-3}} ===In the first anime=== Although following the series storyline to an extent, the first anime's storyline diverts with Edward learning the secret to destroying a [[homunculus]] during his encounter with Greed, whom he kills in an effort to save Alphonse.{{cite episode|title=Theory of Avarice|airdate=November 5, 2005|number=34|credits=Director: Seiji Mizushima|series=Fullmetal Alchemist|series-link=Fullmetal Alchemist|network=Cartoon Network}} When he learns of Scar's creation of a Philosopher's Stone within Alphonse, Edward saves the people of Lior from being sacrificed for its creation.{{cite episode|title=His Name Is Unknown|airdate=January 14, 2006|number=42|credits=Director: Seiji Mizushima|series=Fullmetal Alchemist|series-link=Fullmetal Alchemist|network=Cartoon Network}} During his battle against the homunculi, Edward is killed by [[List of Fullmetal Alchemist characters#Envy|Envy]], who is revealed to be Edward and Alphose's half-brother, but Alphonse trades himself for his brother's revival. In doing so, however, Alphonse's armor with the philosopher's stone within it is used up and he disappears. After being revived, Edward sacrifices his own life to bring back his brother in exchange. As a result, Edward finds himself on the other side of the Gate, a [[Parallel universe (fiction)|parallel world]] which greatly resembles the real world during [[World War II]], while Alphonse recovers his original body. Determined to return to Alphonse, Edward becomes involved in rocketry research in [[Germany]], with the intention of using that technology to return to his home world.{{cite episode|title=Laws and Promises|airdate=March 18, 2006|number=51|credits=Director: Seiji Mizushima|series=Fullmetal Alchemist|series-link=Fullmetal Alchemist|network=Cartoon Network}} In the feature film, ''[[Fullmetal Alchemist the Movie: Conqueror of Shamballa]]'', set two years after the end of the anime, Edward has been living in Germany and looks for a way to return to his world. At the film's end, he decides to stay in the parallel world along with Alphonse so that they may try to protect both worlds.{{cite video|people=Mizushima, Seiji (Director) |date=July 23, 2005 |url=http://www.sonymusic.co.jp/Animation/hagaren/hagaren-movie/index.html |title=Fullmetal Alchemist the Movie: Conqueror of Shambala |medium=Motion picture |location=Japan |publisher=Bones |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070318042714/http://www.sonymusic.co.jp/Animation/hagaren/hagaren-movie/index.html |archive-date=March 18, 2007 }} ===In other media=== Edward also appears in almost all the [[List of Fullmetal Alchemist episodes#OVAs|''Fullmetal Alchemist'' original video animations]] (OVAs). alchemy: the monstrosity of reading words and pictures in shonen manga'', Lesley-Anne Gallacher addressed how the backstory of Edward and Alphonse's failed attempt to revive their mother relate to Shou Tucker's plan to combine his daughter Nina and dog into a monster named chimera. Nevertheless, Alphonse later reacts violently too once understanding the identity of the chimera. As a result, the writer believes the story "weaken the boundaries between different realms of representation is to compromise the integrity of them all".{{cite journal |last=Gallacher |first=Lesley-Anne |year=2011 |title=(Fullmetal) alchemy: the monstrosity of reading words and pictures in shonen manga |journal=Cultural Geographies |volume=18 |issue=4 |pages=457–473 |doi=10.1177/1474474010397639 |bibcode=2011CuGeo..18..457G |s2cid=191476902 |url=http://nrl.northumbria.ac.uk/16596/3/Fullmetal_alchemy.pdf |access-date=2019-01-01 |archive-date=2023-08-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829220030/http://nrl.northumbria.ac.uk/id/eprint/16596/3/Fullmetal_alchemy.pdf |url-status=live }} {{ill|Piotr Konieczny (sociologist)|lt=Piotr Konieczny|pl|Piotr Konieczny (socjolog)}} in ''[[The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction]]'' said both Mustang and Edward reject metaphysical consolation", and instead claim that humans must confrot suffering and injustice while obtaining resposibilty, knowledge and action.{{cite web|last=Konieczny|first=Piotr|date=June 2, 2026|title=Fullmetal Alchemist|url=https://sf-encyclopedia.com/entry/fullmetal_alchemist|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction}} Julie Sadlier from [[York University]] notes how complex is Edward's case of disability despite being a [[Ableism#Supercrip stereotype|supercrip]] through his automail; despite acquiring these metallic limbs, Edward still feels at traumatized from his past and searches for a way to recover his lost arm and leg. Sadlier further commented on Edward's past, comparing it with Ishvalian's civil war who also suffered a tragic loss, most notably the antagonistic Scar who also lost his arm. Other foils noticed by the writer are Lan Fan who amputated herself to aid Ling Yao while noting that through his automail, Arakawa managed to link Edward with Alphonse and Winry.{{cite journal |last= Sadlier|first=Julie|year=2013 |title=Embodiment, Disability and Social Violence in Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood|journal= Beneath the Surface|url=https://surface.syr.edu/bts_conf/2013/Presentations/4/ |access-date=July 14, 2018 }} Tien-yi Chao from Intellect commented on Edward's characterization in the film ''Conqueror of Shamballa''. Across the movie, Edward meets parallel version of people he met including Maes Hughes (a Nazi soldier with the same name) and King Bradley, (a Jewish film director named [[Fritz Lang]]), who behave differently from their Amestris counterparts. Chao addresses that through this exchanges the film also parallels itself from Arakawa's original work that takes a different path in terms of story. Nevertheless, Edward also faces the idea of going back to Amestris and comes in terms with Earth during the climax: in confrontation to Exckhart from the [[Thule Society]], Edward notes that both worlds share similar issues, most notably wars which might become easier to occur if the worlds are connected. As a result, Edward and Alphonse decide to live in the real world in order to protect it from nuclear weapons mentioned across the story.{{cite journal |last= Chao|first=Tien-yi|year=2013 |title=Transmutation of worlds: Adaptation and transformation in Fullmetal Alchemist the Movie: Conqueror of Shamballa|journal= Studies in Comics|volume=4|pages=159–170|publisher=Intellect |doi=10.1386/stic.4.1.159_1}} ==References== {{reflist|30em}} {{Fullmetal Alchemist}} {{good article}} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Elric, Edward}} [[Category:Anime and manga characters introduced in 2001]] [[Category:Cyborg characters in comics]] [[Category:Fictional characters who use magic]] [[Category:Fictional amputees]] [[Category:Fictional atheists and agnostics]] [[Category:Fictional characters who are illegitimate]] [[Category:Fictional characters with post-traumatic stress disorder]] [[Category:Fictional child prodigies]] [[Category:Fictional child soldiers]] [[Category:Fictional cyborgs]] [[Category:Fictional homeless people]] [[Category:Fictional majors]] [[Category:Fullmetal Alchemist characters]] [[Category:Male characters in anime and manga]] [[Category:Fictional martial artists in anime and manga]] [[Category:Orphan characters in anime and manga]] [[Category:Teenage characters in anime and manga]] [[Category:Fictional military personnel in anime and manga]]

[[Fray Tormenta]] | debut = {{dts|1998|4|30}} | retired = }} '''Luis Ignacio Urive Alvirde''' (born December 22, 1982), better known by his [[ring name]] '''Místico''' (Spanish for "Mystic"), is a Mexican [[Professional wrestling|professional wrestler]]. He is signed to both the Mexican [[professional wrestling promotion|promotion]] [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL), where he is the current [[CMLL World Light Heavyweight Championship|CMLL World Light Heavyweight Champion]] and one-third of the [[CMLL World Trios Championship|CMLL World Trios Champions]] with [[Máscara Dorada II|Máscara Dorada]] and [[Neón (wrestler)|Neón]] as El Sky Team, and the American [[Promotion (wrestling)|promotion]] [[All Elite Wrestling]] (AEW). He also makes appearances for [[Major League Wrestling]] (MLW), [[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]] (NJPW), where he is one-half of the current [[IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champions]] with [[El Desperado (wrestler)|El Desperado]] in their first reign as a team and Mistico's first individual reign, and [[Ring of Honor]] (ROH). where he is one-half of the [[ROH World Tag Team Championship|ROH World Tag Team Champions]] with Máscara Dorada. From 2006 to 2011, Urive was the top ''[[Face (professional wrestling)|técnico]]'' (those that portray the "good guys") and biggest box office draw in Mexico for a number of years. Despite having worked under previous ring names, he gained popularity in CMLL as Místico, a religious character who was the [[Kayfabe|storyline]] protégé of the professional wrestling priest [[Fray Tormenta]]. Between 2011 and 2014, he worked for WWE under the ring name '''Sin Cara''' (Spanish for "Without Face" or "Faceless"; after which, his ring name was given to his storyline rival [[Cinta de Oro|Hunico]]). Urive then worked for [[Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide]] (AAA), adopting the name '''Myzteziz''', and returned to CMLL in 2015 under the name '''Carístico'''.{{efn|The name is a [[portmanteau]] of his two most well known names " Místico" and "Sin Cara".}} In 2021, he regained the Místico name, due to his successor and tag team partner [[Dralístico|Místico II]] leaving CMLL. On two occasions in 2008, Místico held five championships simultaneously and has won most major CMLL championships over the years, as well as CMLL's ''[[CMLL Torneo Gran Alternativa|Torneo Gran Alternativa]]'' and ''[[Leyenda de Plata]]'' tournaments on three occasions each. Urive is the son of Miguel Urive, who wrestled under the ring name [[Dr. Karonte]], the brother of wrestlers Astro Boy, Argos, [[Argenis (wrestler)|Argenis]] and Dr. Karonte Jr, the cousin of wrestlers [[Magnus (luchador)|Magnus]] and Ulises Jr. as well as the nephew of CMLL booker [[Tony Salazar]].{{Professional wrestling sidebar}} == Personal life == While most masked professional wrestlers do not reveal their real name unless they are unmasked in a ''[[Lucha libre#Luchas de Apuestas|Lucha de Apuestas]]'' ("bet match"), Luis Ignacio Urive Alvirde's full name was revealed by WWE when they released Urive from his contract in 2014.{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/inside/wwe-releases-luis-ignacio-urive-alvirde-26215470|title=WWE releases Luis Ignacio Urive Alvirde|date=March 27, 2014|publisher=[[WWE]]|access-date=April 26, 2014 | archive-date=March 28, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328223401/http://www.wwe.com/inside/wwe-releases-luis-ignacio-urive-alvirde-26215470}} Urive was born on December 22, 1982, in Mexico City, Mexico, the son of Miguel Urive, who was a professional wrestler known under the name "[[Dr. Karonte]]". He is one of at least five of Miguel Urive's sons to become a professional wrestler.{{efn|Unless a luchador has been unmasked as a result of a match, his birth name is normally not revealed to the general public, leading to the possibility that other sons or daughters are wrestling.}} His older brother worked under the name "Astro Boy" until his death in the late 1990s. His younger brothers work as the masked wrestlers Argos, [[Argenis (wrestler)|Argenis]], and Karonte Jr.{{cite book|author=Madigan|title=Mondo Lucha a Go Go: the bizarre & honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling|publisher=HarperCollins|year=2007|chapter=A family affair|pages=128–132|isbn=978-0-06-085583-3|first=Dan}}{{cite web|url=http://www.wrestleview.com/viewnews.php?id=1314399534|title=Viva La Raza! Lucha Weekly|last=Boutwell|first=Josh|date=August 26, 2011|access-date=October 23, 2012|website=WrestleView | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110830101649/http://www.wrestleview.com/viewnews.php?id=1314399534 | archive-date=August 30, 2011}} Urive's uncle, [[Tony Salazar]], is a retired wrestler who ended up working for [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL) as both a trainer and a booker. Salazar's son, [[Magnus (luchador)|Magnus]], also works for CMLL.{{cite web|url=http://www.cmll.com/forjandounidolo/delta/magnus/index.html |title=Magnus |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029200359/http://www.cmll.com/forjandounidolo/delta/magnus/index.html |archive-date=October 29, 2013 |access-date=October 21, 2012 |publisher=[[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] |work=Forjando un Idolo |language=es |url-status=dead }} == Professional wrestling career == === Early career (1998–2003) === After training under his father and uncle, Urive made his professional wrestling debut as "Dr. Karonte, Jr." on April 30, 1998, at the age of 15. In 2000, he changed his ring name to "Astro Boy" in honor of his older brother, who previously used the name and had died months earlier. He later formed a [[tag team]] with another brother who worked as "Astro Boy II". In 2003, he traveled to Japan to work for [[Michinoku Pro Wrestling]], where he was billed as "Komachi", a [[Glossary of professional wrestling terms#Gimmick|ring persona]] he took over from fellow professional wrestler [[Volador Jr.]], who had played the part for about a year.{{cite news|title=Número Especial - Lo mejor de la lucha libre mexicana durante el 2003|work= [[Súper Luchas]] |id=Issue 40|date=January 5, 2003|language=es | trans-title= Special Edition: The best of Mexican wrestling in 2003}} === Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (2004–2011) === ==== Rise to stardom (2004–2009) ==== In 2004, CMLL repackaged Urive as Místico, giving him an elaborate backstory to go with his new persona. Místico (the character) was an orphan taken in by the wrestling priest [[Fray Tormenta]], who taught him to wrestle; CMLL's previous attempt at this storyline with [[El Sagrado]] failed to take off.{{cite book | author= Madigan | title= Mondo Lucha Libre: the bizarre & honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling | publisher= HarperCollins Publishers | year= 2007 | chapter = What's in a name | pages = 215–223 | isbn= 978-0-06-085583-3|first=Dan}} He began teaming with Volador Jr. and [[Misterioso Jr.|Misterioso II]] on the second or third match of the [[Glossary of professional wrestling terms#Card|card]]. On July 16, he participated in the ''[[Leyenda de Plata#Leyenda de Plata 2004|Leyenda de Plata]]'' ("The Silver Legend") tournament, eliminating [[Virus (wrestler)|Virus]] before being eliminated by [[Toscano (wrestler)|Tarzan Boy]] in the first round.{{cite web|url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/emll/silver.html#2004|title=Leyenda de Plata 2004|date=July 16–30, 2004|access-date=August 16, 2009|publisher=Pro Wrestling History|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101128153925/http://prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/emll/silver.html#2004|archive-date=November 28, 2010|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} Later that year, he won the ''[[CMLL Torneo Gran Alternativa#2004|Torneo Gran Alternativa]]'' ("Great Alternative Tournament") with veteran [[El Hijo del Santo]], after which he was nicknamed ''El Principe de Plata y Oro'' ("The Prince of Silver and Gold"), a reference to the main colors of his outfits. Shortly afterward, the [[Glossary of professional wrestling terms#Book|bookers]] began teaming him with other established [[Face (professional wrestling)|''técnicos'' (faces)]], such as [[Negro Casas]] and [[Shocker (wrestler)|Shocker]], against the top [[Heel (professional wrestling)|''rúdo'' (heel)]] [[Glossary of professional wrestling terms#Stable|groups]] ''[[Los Guerreros del Infierno]]'' and ''[[La Furia del Norte]]''. His stature made him an [[underdog]], and his high-flying moves, such as diving arm-drags, made him popular with [[Arena México]] crowds. [[File:Místico.jpg|left|thumb|Místico in 2006|262x262px]] Místico won his first title on January 1, 2005, defeating [[Averno (wrestler)|Averno]] for the [[NWA World Middleweight Championship]]; the match was well received by the audience, who threw [[money]] into the ring as a sign of appreciation. Two weeks later, he defeated ''Los Guerreros del Infierno'' leader [[Último Guerrero]] in his first singles main event match. After a brief program pitting him and [[Dr. Wagner Jr.]] against Guerrero and [[Rey Bucanero]], Místico [[Feud (professional wrestling)|feuded]] with [[Perro Aguayo Jr.]] and his group, ''[[Los Perros del Mal]]'' ([[Damián 666]], [[Halloween (wrestler)|Halloween]] and [[Héctor Garza]]). On June 17, they were involved in an eight-man [[Professional wrestling match types#Cages|cage match]] where the last man in the cage lost his hair or mask. Neither man was involved in the finish, where Damián pinned [[Máscara Mágica II|Máscara Mágica]]. During the third fall of a match with Guerrero in September, he was attacked by now-''rúdo'' [[Atlantis (wrestler)|Atlantis]], whom he defeated in October.{{cite news|title=Lucha Libre: Conoce la historia de las leyendas de cuadrilátero|work=Atlantis (1962)|location=[[Mexico]]|id=Grandes Figuras de la Lucha Libre|page=8|year=2008|language=es}} Místico was the biggest star in Mexico at the start of 2006, working eighteen main event matches that drew more than ten thousand people; the ''[[Wrestling Observer Newsletter]]'''s "Year-End Awards" voted him "Performer of the Year", "Biggest Box Office Draw" and "Best Flying Wrestler". He feuded with [[Black Warrior (wrestler)|Black Warrior]], who [[Glossary of professional wrestling terms#Turn|turned]] on him during a [[CMLL World Tag Team Championship]] match. Místico lost his NWA World Middleweight Championship to Warrior on May 12, but defeated him in a mask vs. mask ''Lucha de Apuestas'' in the main event of the [[CMLL 73rd Anniversary Show]] on September 29, ending their feud.{{cite news|title=Enciclopedia de las Mascaras|work=Black Warrior|location=Mexico|id=Tomo I|page=35|date=July 2007|language=es|trans-title= Encyclopedia of Masks}} In early 2007, [[WWE|World Wrestling Entertainment]] (WWE) reportedly offered Místico a contract, which he could not sign due to commitments with CMLL at the time; the likes of [[Dean Malenko]], [[Paul London]] and [[Rey Mysterio]] had pushed WWE to offer him a deal. On February 27, he wrestled a tryout match against Malenko and [[Jamie Noble]] prior to [[WWE SmackDown|''SmackDown!'']] in [[San Jose, California]].{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Mike |date=February 27, 2026 |title=2/27 this day in history: WWE NXT Arrival becomes first ever live WWE Network special, Hulk Hogan appreciation night at MSG, Gorilla vs. Bruno in the Garden, Steve Bradley wins Super 8 and more |url=https://www.pwinsider.com/article/99972/227-this-day-in-history-wwe-nxt-arrival-becomes-first-ever-live-wwe-network-special-hulk-hogan-appreciation-night-at-msg-gorilla-vs-bruno-in-the-garden-steve-bradley-wins-super-8-and-more.html?p=1 |access-date=April 20, 2026 |website=Pro Wrestling Insider |quote=Prior to the event, CMLL wrestler Mistico received a tryout in the empty arena. He wrestled Dean Malenko and Jamie Noble.}} On April 10, Místico defeated [[Mephisto (wrestler)|Mephisto]] for the [[CMLL World Welterweight Championship]]. On March 10, 2008, Místico and Garza defeated Averno and Mephisto for the tag team championship. Místico had also contacted [[Total Nonstop Action Wrestling]] (TNA) about a potential deal, yet his CMLL commitment kept the parties from reaching one.{{Cite web |last=Csonka |first=Larry |author-link=Larry Csonka (journalist) |date=March 11, 2008 |title=TNA News: TNA Live, Mistico to TNA and More |url=https://411mania.com/wrestling/tna-news-tna-live-mistico-to-tna-and-more/ |access-date=August 16, 2009 |website=411Mania}} When the commission declared the title vacant after a match ended in a double disqualification, Místico and Garza regained then lost it back to them in December.{{cite news|author=Rosas Plata|title=El centro, vacante... !otra vez!|work=Ovaciones|publisher=Editorial Ovaciones, S. A. de C.V.|location=Mexico, [[Mexican Federal District|D.F.]]|id=Número 21200 Año LXI|page=22|date=May 24, 2008|language=es | trans-title= The Championship, vacant... again!|first=Arturo}}{{cite news|author=Rosas Plata|title=Místico y Garza, de nuevo campeones|work=Ovaciones|publisher=Editorial Ovaciones, S. A. de C.V.|location=Mexico, [[Mexican Federal District|D.F.]]|id=Número 21235 Año LXI|page=22|date=May 24, 2008|language=es | trans-title=Místico and Garza, the new champions|first=Arturo}}{{cite news|title=Lo Mejor de la Lucha Libre Mexicana 2008|work= [[Súper Luchas]] |id=296|date=January 6, 2008 |language=es | trans-title=The best of Mexican wrestling 2008}} Místico lost his championship to Casas at ''[[Homenaje a Dos Leyendas (2009)|Homenaje a Dos Leyendas]]'' ("Homage to Two Legends") on March 18, 2009, failing to regain it on April 12.{{cite news|author=Flores|title=Cayó la máscara de Villano V|location=Mexico|id=307|pages=3–7|work= [[Súper Luchas]] |date=March 23, 2009|first=Manuel|first2=Manuel|last2=Rivera|language=es|trans-title=Villano V lost his mask}}{{Cite web |last=Miguel |first=Jose |date=April 13, 2009 |title=CMLL - Arena México (Resultados 12 abr ’09): Domingo Familiar: Marcela destapa a Rosa Negra |trans-title=CMLL - Arena Mexico (Results 12 Apr '09): Family Sunday: Marcela unmasks Rosa Negra |url=https://superluchas.com/cmll-arena-mexico-resultados-12-abr-2009-domingo-familiar-marcela-destapa-a-rosa-negra-jessica-dayana-hernandez-originaria-del-df/ |access-date=August 6, 2026 |website=[[Súper Luchas]] |language=es}} He participated in the [[CMLL Universal Championship (2009)|Universal Championship]] tournament on June 12, defeating [[Ephesto]] in the first round and Garza in the quarter-finals, before losing to Guerrero in the semi-finals.{{Cite web |last=Rivera |first=Manuel |date=June 13, 2009 |title=CMLL Arena México (12 junio '09): Último Guerrero, segundo finalista al Campeonato Universal |trans-title=CMLL Arena Mexico (June 12, 2009): Último Guerrero, runner-up for the Universal Championship |url=https://superluchas.com/cmll-arena-mexico-12-junio-2009-ultimo-guerrero-es-el-segundo-finalista-al-campeonato-universal-shocker-gana-por-descalificacion-a-dos-caras-jr/ |access-date=June 11, 2026 |website=[[Súper Luchas]] |language=es}} The feud between Místico and Casas culminated in a ''Lucha de Apuestas'' in the main event of the [[CMLL 76th Anniversary Show]] on September 18, which Místico won, resulting in Casas being shaved bald. After the match, Místico made an ''Apuesta'' challenge to [[El Felino]], Casas' cornerman.{{Cite web |date=September 19, 2009 |title=Místico rapó al Negro Casas en 76 Aniversario del CMLL |trans-title=Místico shaved Negro Casas' head at CMLL's 76th Anniversary show |url=https://www.mediotiempo.com/lucha-libre/mistico-rapo-negro-casas-76-aniversario-cmll |access-date=September 19, 2009 |website=MedioTiempo |language=es}}{{Cite web |last=Marquina |first=Alva |date=September 18, 2009 |title=76 Aniversario del CMLL (Cobertura y Resultados en vivo 18 septiembre 2009) – Místico vs Negro Casas – Máscara vs Cabellera |trans-title=76th Anniversary of CMLL (coverage and results live September 18, 2009) – Místico vs Negro Casas – Mask vs Hair |url=https://superluchas.com/76-aniversario-del-cmll-resultados-en-vivo-18-septiembre-2009-mistico-vs-negro-casas-mascara-vs-cabellera/ |access-date=September 19, 2009 |website=[[Súper Luchas]] |language=es}} He and [[Ángel de Oro]] were paired for the [[Torneo Gran Alternativa (2009)|''Torneo Gran Alternativa'']] on September 25, defeating Atlantis and Camorra in the first round and [[Mr. Niebla]] and [[Felino Jr.|Tiger Kid]] in the semi-finals, before losing to [[Shigeo Okumura|Okumura]] and [[Yujiro Takahashi|Yujiro]] in the finals.{{Cite web |last=Marquina |first=Alva |date=September 25, 2009 |title=CMLL - (Resultados en vivo 25 septiembre de 2009): Último Guerrero venció a Liger |trans-title=CMLL - (Live Results September 25, 2009): Último Guerrero defeated Liger |url=https://superluchas.com/cmll-resultados-en-vivo-25-septiembre-de-2009-ultimo-guerrero-vs-liger-torneo-la-gran-alternativa/ |access-date=February 5, 2010 |website=[[Súper Luchas]] |language=es}} ==== Feud with Volador Jr. (2010–2011) ==== [[File:Hector-Garza-vs-Mistico.jpg|thumb|Místico being lifted up by [[Héctor Garza]] in 2010]] On January 22, 2010, Místico and Averno participated in the ''[[CMLL Torneo Nacional de Parejas Increíbles (2010)|Torneo Nacional de Parejas Increibles]]'' ("National Incredible Pairs Tournament"), where a ''técnico'' is paired with a ''rúdo''; they wore matching outfits and defeated [[Euforia (wrestler)|Euforia]] and Ephesto in the first round. Místico seemingly developed a ''rúdo'' attitude in the quarter-finals, attacking Volador Jr. and going so far as to ripping up his mask, performing an illegal low blow on him for the win. Afterward, he took the microphone and commented that "all was fair in war and defending Mexico City", drawing many boos from the crowd. Místico continued working a ''rúdo'' style in the semi-finals, but he and Averno lost to Atlantis and [[Gran Metalik|Máscara Dorada]].{{Cite web |last=Velázquez |first=Israel |date=January 23, 2010 |title=CMLL en la Arena México (Viernes 22 de enero 2010) – ¿Místico se vuelve rudo? |trans-title=CMLL at Arena Mexico (Friday, January 22, 2010) – Is Místico turning heel? |url=https://superluchas.com/cmll-en-la-arena-mexico-viernes-22-de-enero-2010-mistico-se-vuelve-rudo/ |access-date=January 28, 2010 |website=[[Súper Luchas]] |language=es}}{{Cite web |last=Boutwell |first=Josh |date=January 29, 2010 |title=Viva La Raza! Lucha Weekly |url=https://www.wrestleview.com/uncategorized/1791-viva-la-raza-lucha-weekly-9/ |access-date=January 29, 2010 |website=WrestleView}} Volador Jr. then challenged him to a ''Super Libre'' (no rules) match if Místico would agree to it.{{Cite web |last=Ruiz Glez |first=Alex |date=January 26, 2010 |title=Volador Jr. quiere un mano a mano en súper libre contra Místico |trans-title=Volador Jr. wants a one-on-one Super Libre match against Místico |url=https://superluchas.com/volador-jr-quiere-un-mano-a-mano-en-super-libre-contra-mistico-se-aproxima-la-respuesta-del-cmll-a-los-perros-del-mal/ |access-date=January 28, 2010 |website=[[Súper Luchas]] |language=es}} During a match between the two on February 5, Místico was clearly a ''rúdo'', tearing so viciously at Volador Jr.'s mask that a new one had to be brought to the ring between falls. ''[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]'' noted that his ''La Mística'' finishing move was often executed so fast that his opponents did not have time to react until it was locked in.{{cite news|title=Pro Wrestling Illustrated 500 – 2008: 17 Mistico|work=[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]|publisher=Sports and Entertainment publications LLC|location=Blue Bell, [[Pennsylvania]], [[United States]]|id=October 2008|page=50|date=August 2008}} ''La Mística'' is, in reality, a series of moves used by many wrestlers over the years, but Urive's version is a combination of the spinning [[Professional wrestling holds#Tilt-a-whirl|tilt-a-whirl]] [[Professional wrestling throws#Headscissors takedown|headscissors]] takedown transitioned into a [[Professional wrestling throws#Armbar takedown|single arm DDT]] that brings his opponent to the mat, allowing him to instantly switch the move into a [[Professional wrestling holds#Fujiwara armbar|fujiwara armbar]], normally on the opponent's left arm, that would force them to submit. The "La Mística" move became so synonymous with the Místico character that Urive's successor also adopted it as his finishing move.{{cite web|url=http://cmll.com/02_resultados/dom_arena_mex/dom_arenamex.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130620150440/http://www.cmll.com/02_resultados/dom_arena_mex/dom_arenamex.htm |title=Resultados Arena México Domingo 16 de Junio '13 |last=Salazar López |first=Alexis A. |archive-date=June 20, 2013 |date=June 17, 2013 |access-date=June 17, 2013 |work=[[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] |language=es | trans-title= Arena Mexico Results, Sunday June 16, 13 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web|url=http://cmll.com/02_resultados/super_viernes/super_viernes_cmll.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130917012751/http://www.cmll.com/02_resultados/super_viernes/super_viernes_cmll.htm |title=Resultados Arena México Viernes 13 de Septiembre '13 |last=Salazar López |first=Alexis A. |archive-date=September 17, 2013 |date=September 14, 2013 |access-date=September 14, 2013 |work=[[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] |language=es | trans-title= Arena Mexico Results, Friday September 13, 13|url-status=dead }} Urive occasionally used the move while working as Sin Cara and made it his main finishing move after returning to Mexico. As Sin Cara, he used a [[Moonsault#Moonsault side slam|moonsault side slam]] and [[Professional wrestling aerial techniques#Senton bomb|senton bomb]] as his finishing moves, both of which are executed off the top rope; for the moonsault side slam, an opponent was thrown off the top rope, with Urive landing on top of the opponent, while the senton sees Urive leap off the top rope onto a prone opponent.{{cite web|url=http://pwtorch.com/artman2/publish/wwerawreport/article_64825.shtml|title=Caldwell's WWE Raw results 9/3: Ongoing "virtual-time" coverage of live Raw – Punk returns home, Anger Management|last=Caldwell|first=James|date=September 3, 2012|access-date=September 4, 2012|publisher=Pro Wrestling Torch|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121030030148/http://pwtorch.com/artman2/publish/wwerawreport/article_64825.shtml|archive-date=October 30, 2012|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}} Throughout his career, Urive has primarily portrayed a ''técnico'' (heroic) character, with brief periods where he played a more ambiguous character who straddled the ''técnico''/''rúdo'' divide. When introduced as Místico in 2004, CMLL created an elaborate fictional backstory, where he was an orphan who was taught to wrestle by Fray Tormenta, a wrestling priest who also acted as his ''Padrino'' ("Godfather"). As part of the religious backstory, Místico would often pose with his hands put together in a "praying" motion and adorn his tights with crucifix like patterns. Early in his career, he wore mainly white trunks and masks with either silver or gold adornment, earning him the nickname "''El Príncipe de Plata y Oro''" ("The Prince of Silver and Gold").{{cite web|url=http://superluchas.com/infierno-en-el-ring-74-aniversario-de-la-arena-mexico/|title=Infierno en el ring, 74 aniversario de la arena mexico|author=Ocampo|date=September 24, 2007|access-date=July 19, 2011|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|language=es|trans-title=Inferno in the Ring, the 74th anniversary of Arena Mexico|archive-date=August 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180815164850/https://superluchas.com/infierno-en-el-ring-74-aniversario-de-la-arena-mexico/|url-status=live|first=Jorge}} The Místico mask only has eye holes, totally covering the nose, mouth and ears, a design that was replicated in the masks Urive wore as Sin Cara, Myzteziz and Carístico, with variations on the design that adorn the mask. The Carístico mask retains the same basic design as Místico, but with an added crucifix on the forehead and sweeping wing design around the eye openings.{{cite web | url=http://www.record.com.mx/lucha-cmll/caristico-dispuesto-apostar-su-mascara-contra-mistico | title=Carístico, dispuesto a apostar su Máscara contra Místico | date=April 11, 2018 | access-date=November 23, 2018 | work=[[Récord (Mexican newspaper)|Récord]] | language=es | trans-title=Carístico, willing to bet his mask against Místico | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181124003739/http://www.record.com.mx/lucha-cmll/caristico-dispuesto-apostar-su-mascara-contra-mistico | archive-date=November 24, 2018 | url-status=live }} In 2006 and 2007, readers of the ''Wrestling Observer Newsletter'' voted him the "[[List of Wrestling Observer Newsletter awards#Best Flying Wrestler|Best Flying Wrestler]]" based on his in-ring performance in Mexico.{{Citation|last=Meltzer|first=Dave|author-link=Dave Meltzer|date=January 22, 2007|title=2006 Wrestling Observer Newsletter Awards|periodical=[[Wrestling Observer Newsletter]]|publication-place=Campbell, CA|pages=1–12|issn=1083-9593}} He was ranked third in ''[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]'''s list of the top 500 wrestlers of 2007. However, his reputation as a wrestler in Mexico contrasted with his work in WWE. He developed a reputation of being prone to not being able to execute some of the high-risk/high-flying moves, labeling the problems as "[[botch (professional wrestling)|botching]]" the moves, which followed him for the entire three years of his WWE career.{{cite web | url=https://www.f4wonline.com/wwe-news/wwe-can-make-la-sombra-top-star-if-they-want-learn-past-mistakes-202871 | title=WWE can make La Sombra a top star if they want to learn from past mistakes | first=Kyle | last=Johnson | work=[[Wrestling Observer Newsletter]] | access-date=May 1, 2019 | date=December 3, 2015 | archive-date=May 2, 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190502224615/https://www.f4wonline.com/wwe-news/wwe-can-make-la-sombra-top-star-if-they-want-learn-past-mistakes-202871 | url-status=dead }} Former WWE producer [[Arn Anderson]] stated that: "this guy didn't show me anything. Not a damn thing. He had a bad attitude."{{Cite web |last=Beltrán |first=William |date=February 26, 2021 |title=Arn Anderson: "Sin Cara (Carístico) falló en WWE. Tenía mala actitud" |trans-title=Arn Anderson: "Sin Cara (Carístico) failed in WWE. He had a bad attitude" |url=https://superluchas.com/arn-anderson-sin-cara-caristico-fallo-wwe-mala-actitud/ |access-date=October 12, 2021 |website=[[Súper Luchas]] |language=es}} Rey Mysterio said during an interview that Urive did not "have the desire" to be in WWE.{{Cite web |date=April 5, 2014 |title=Le faltaron ganas a Sin Cara: Rey Mysterio |trans-title=Sin Cara lacked the desire: Rey Mysterio |url=https://www.mediotiempo.com/lucha-libre/wwe/le-faltaron-ganas-a-sin-cara-rey-mysterio |access-date=October 12, 2021 |website=MedioTiempo |language=es}} Jorge Arriaga, who took the [[Cinta de Oro|Sin Cara]] character when Urive was fired, said that "[the original Sin Cara] is the biggest signing that [[Triple H|he]] had from Mexico.
