'''Fuerza Guerrera'''{{Notetag|[[Spanish language|Spanish]] for "Warrior Strength". Not to be mistaken for the surname [[Guerrero wrestling family|Guerrero]].}} (born December 13, 1953) is the [[ring name]] of a Mexican [[professional wrestler]]. Throughout his career, Guerrera has worked for every major [[professional wrestling promotion]] in Mexico including [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL), [[Lucha Libre AAA World Wide]] (AAA), the [[Universal Wrestling Association]] (UWA), the [[World Wrestling Association]] (WWA), and the [[International Wrestling Revolution Group]] (IWRG), holding [[championship (professional wrestling)|championships]] including the [[CMLL World Trios Championship]], [[CMLL World Welterweight Championship]], [[Mexican National Lightweight Championship]], [[Mexican National Middleweight Championship]], [[Mexican National Tag Team Championship]], [[Mexican National Trios Championship]], [[Mexican National Welterweight Championship]], and [[NWA World Welterweight Championship]]. His son, [[Juventud Guerrera]], is also a professional wrestler.

==Professional wrestling career==

===Early eareer (1977–1981)===
The wrestler who would become known as Fuerza Guerrera trained for his professional wrestling career under Dick Angelo, he would later receive further training from Gallo Tapado, [[Raul Reyes]], [[El Solar]], [[El Espectro]] and [[Ángel Blanco]].<ref name=FuerzaProfile>{{cite news|title=Guerreros | work = Un aniversario más de Fuerza Guerrera|location=San Borja [[Mexico]] | id = Año 4 #170 | pages = 16–21 | publisher= Editorial Magno, S.A. C.V. C.P. | date= December 2008|language=es}}</ref> He made his professional wrestling debut in 1977 under the [[ring name]] Cachorro González (Spanish for "Cub González").<ref name=FuerzaProfile/> in his debut match he faced, and lost to, Rokambole (later [[Villano V]]) and Leopardo Negro ([[Villano IV]]) in San Pedro, Puebla.<ref name=FuerzaProfile/> After wrestling as Chachorro González for over a year González wanted to adopt an ''enmascarado'' character by the name of "Star Wars", but the local promoter, Señor Barradas, did not want wrestlers with English names. Instead he adopted the name "Fuerza Guerrera", a name he came up with inspired by the Aztec warriors of Latin America. Fuerza Guerrera also adopted a black mask with red and blue markings – red representing passion and blue representing peace, a mask that quickly became his trademark.<ref name=FuerzaProfile/> He made his in-ring debut as Fuerza Guerrera on December 19, 1979, in ''Arena Naucalpan''.<ref name=FuerzaProfile/> Since his debut Guerrera has almost always worked as a ''Rudo'', a "bad guy" or "[[Heel (professional wrestling)|Heel]]" character, a choice he took early on as it fit with both his personality and his wrestling style.

===Empresa Mexicana de Lucha Libre (1981–1992)===
The combination of Guerrera's in-ring skills, natural charisma and unique mask quickly landed him a regular job working for [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre|Empresa Mexicana de Lucha Libre]] (EMLL), Mexico's largest wrestling promotion.<ref name=FuerzaProfile/> On September 25, 1981, Fuerza Guerrera made his first appearance at a major EMLL show as he wrestled and defeated [[Negro Casas]] on EMLL's 48th Anniversary show.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/emll/anniversary50.html#48|title= 48th Anniversary Show | date= September 25, 1981 | access-date= January 7, 2010 | publisher=Pro Wrestling History}}</ref> On November 6, 1983, Guerrera defeated Aguila Venezolana in a tournament final to win the vacant [[Mexican National Lightweight Championship]], the first professional wrestling championships of his career.<ref name=MexLight/> In May, 1984 Guerrera vacated the title when he moved from the [[Lucha Libre#Weight classes|lightweight weight class]] (between {{convert|63|kg|lb|abbr=on}} and {{convert|70|kg|lb|abbr=on}}) and into the [[Lucha Libre#Weight classes|Welterweight weight class]] (between {{convert|70|kg|lb|abbr=on}} and {{convert|78|kg|lb|abbr=on}}).<ref name="WeightDivision">{{cite web| url= http://www.ordenjuridico.gob.mx/Estatal/ESTADO%20DE%20MEXICO/Reglamentos/MEXREG004.pdf | title= Reglamento de Box y Lucha Libre Professional del Estado de Mexico | author= Arturo Montiel Rojas | publisher= Comisión de Box y Lucha Libre Mexico D.F. | date= August 30, 2001 | access-date= January 7, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061130181418/http://www.ordenjuridico.gob.mx/Estatal/ESTADO%20DE%20MEXICO/Reglamentos/MEXREG004.pdf|archive-date=November 30, 2006}}</ref> On December 3, 1985, Fuerza Guerrera captured the [[Mexican National Welterweight Championship]] when he defeated Javier Cruz.<ref name=MexWelter/> Guerrera held the title for approximately 240 days before vacating the title as he left EMLL to work for other wrestling promotions in Mexico.<ref name=MexWelter/> By late 1988 Guerrera had returned to EMLL and captured the [[NWA World Welterweight Championship]] on October 4, 1988, when he defeated Solar II and won the highest ranking title in the Welterweight division at the time.<ref name=NWAWelter/> Guerrera would go on to make several successful title defenses until he lost to [[Águila Solitaria]] on June 2, 1980. Guerrera regained the title three days later and went on to have an 808-day reign that included successful title defenses against [[Pantera (wrestler)|Pantera II]], [[Americo Rocca]], his trainer Gallo Tapado, [[Misterioso (wrestler)|Misterioso]] and [[Octagón]]. In 1989 Guerrera also began working part-time in the [[Tijuana]], [[Baja California]] based [[World Wrestling Association]] promotion, winning the WWA Welterweight Championship twice in 1989 and 1990.<ref name=WWAWelter/>

During his title reign Fuerza Guerrera began a long running [[narrative thread|storyline]] feud that quickly drew big crowds as the two talented young wrestlers worked a series of very highly thought off matches.<ref name=FuerzaProfile/> On December 14, 1990, Fuerza Guerrera and Octagón were involved in a three-way ''[[Lucha libre#Luchas de Apuestas|Luchas de Apuesta]]'' ("bet match"), round robin tournament along with [[Huracán Ramírez]] where their masks were on the line. In the end Guerrera managed to defeat both Octagón and Ramírez, forcing the two to face off with their mask on the line. Guerrera sat on the sideline and watched Octagón defeat Ramírez and unmask him after the match per Lucha Libre traditions.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Lucha Libre: Conoce la historia de las leyendas de cuadrilátero|work=Octagón (1961)|location=[[Mexico]]|id=Grandes Figuras de la Lucha Libre|page=42|year=2008|language=es}}
</ref> On December 15, 1991, Guerrera and Octagón were once again involved in an ''Apuesta'' match where each could potentially lose their mask. The two teamed up to take on [[El Hijo del Santo]] and Black Shadow, Jr. in a [[Professional wrestling tag team match types#Parejas Suicidas|''Relevos suicida'' match]], where the losing team is forced to wrestle each other with their mask on the line. Fuerza Guerrera pinned El Hijo del Santo to keep both his and Octagón's mask safe, while Hijo del Santo would go on to unmask Black Shadow, Jr.<ref>{{cite news|title=Guerreros | work = Función del Recuerdo hace 17 anos|location=San Borja, [[Mexico]] | id = Año 4 #170 | pages = 3 | publisher= Editorial Magno, S.A. C.V. C.P.|date=December 2008|language=es}}</ref> On February 15, 1992, Fuerza Guerrera became the first ever [[CMLL World Welterweight Championship|CMLL World Welterweight Champion]] when he defeated El Khalifa in the finals of a [[CMLL World Welterweight Championship#1992 World Light Heavyweight tournament|4-man tournament]].<ref name=CMLLWelter/> Guerrera only held the title for 22 days before losing it to [[Pantera (wrestler)|America]].<ref name=CMLLWelter/>

===Asistencia Asesoría y Administración / AAA (1992–2007)===
In mid 1992 CMLL head booker [[Antonio Peña]] decided to break away from the promotion and start on his own, founding a company called [[Lucha Libre AAA World Wide|Asistencia Asesoría y Administración]], later known simply as AAA. When Peña left CMLL a lot of wrestlers, especially younger wrestlers and lower weight division wrestlers, left with him to AAA, among those to leave was Fuerza Guerrera and his rival Octagón who moved to AAA to continue their feud.<ref name=Pena>{{cite web|url=http://superluchas.com/el-fin-de-una-era/|title=El fin de una era|date=October 7, 2006|access-date=October 14, 2009|author=Ocampo, Ernesto|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|language=es}}</ref> One of Peña's creations was the annual ''Triplemanía'' event, starting with [[Triplemanía I]] on March 30, 1993, where Fuerza Guerrera teamed with [[Erick Casas|Heavy Metal]] and Rambo in a loss to Octagón, El Hijo del Santo and [[Villano III]].<ref name="Trip1">{{cite web|url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/aaa/triple.html#i|title=Asistencia Asesoria y Administracion TripleMania|access-date=January 9, 2010|publisher=Pro Wrestling History}}</ref>

In the months following Triplemanía I Fuerza's son, working under the name [[Juventud Guerrera]], made his debut in AAA and began teaming with his father on a regular basis. On November 6, 1994, Fuerza Guerrera teamed with [[Louie Spicolli|Madonna's Boyfriend]], and [[Psicosis]] to defeat [[Rey Mysterio, Jr.]], Heavy Metal, and [[Latin Lover (wrestler)|Latin Lover]] on the undercard of AAA's first ever [[Pay-Per-View]] ''[[AAA When Worlds Collide]]''.<ref>{{cite news|title=Historical Cards|work=PWI Presents: 2007 Wrestling Almanak and book of facts|publisher=Kappa Publications|id=2007 Edition|page=160}}</ref> On December 2, 1994, Fuerza and Juventud Guerrera defeated Heavy Metal and Latin Lover to win the [[Mexican National Tag Team Championship]], a title the team held for 181 days before losing the belts to Latin Lover and [[Ephesto|Panterita del Ring]].<ref name=MexTag/> The father-son team would also win the [[WWA Tag Team Championship (Mexico)|WWA Tag Team Championship]]{{Notetag|While the [[World Wrestling Association]] was not affiliated with AAA they allowed their titles to be defended on AAA shows.}}<ref name=WWATag/> Los Guerreras also teamed with Psicosos to win the [[WWA Trios Championship (Mexico)|WWA Trios Championship]] from El Hijo del Santo, Octagón and Rey Misterio, Jr.<ref name=WWATrios/> Fuerza Guerrera would also briefly hold the IWC World Middleweight Championship.<ref name=IWCMiddle/> In late 1995 AAA and ''[[Promo Azteca]]'' who had been co-promoting shows for about a year split up and Juventud Guerrera left AAA for Promo Azteca. Following his departure Los Guerreras were stripped of the National tag Team titles<ref name=MexTag/> On September 6, 1996, Fuerza, [[Blue Panther]] and [[El Signo]] won the [[Mexican National Trios Championship]], a title that would soon after become inactive as the three began working for different promotions.<ref name=MexTrios/>

In 1997 Fuerza Guerrera teamed with [[Jerry Estrada]] and Heavy Metal, losing to [[Héctor Garza]], Perro Aguayo and [[El Canek]] at the [[World Wrestling Entertainment|World Wrestling Federations]] (WWF) 1997 [[Royal Rumble (1997)|Royal Rumble]] event, a match that came about due to the AAA/WWF working relationship at the time. This was Guerrera's only WWF appearance.<ref>{{cite news|title=Historical Cards|work=PWI Presents: 2007 Wrestling Almanak and book of facts|publisher=Kappa Publications|id=2007 Edition|page=1640}}</ref> On May 15, 1997, Fuerza Guerrera teamed with [[X-Fly|Mosco de la Merced]] to win the Mexican National Tag Team title for a third time.<ref name=MexTag/> A couple of months later the original Mosco de la Merced left AAA and was quietly replaced by [[Mosco de la Merced II]] who took both the original wrestlers bookings and his half of the Mexican tag team title. The team held the tag team titles until losing to the father/son team of [[Perro Aguayo]] and [[Perro Aguayo, Jr.]] on June 7, 1998.<ref name=MexTag/>

In 2001 Fuerza Guerrera made his return to CMLL, initially to team with Blue Panther and El Signo to lose the Mexican National Trios title to [[Mr. Niebla]], [[Olímpico]] and [[Ephesto|Safari]], handing the titles over to CMLL. In 2002 Guerrera, Blue Panther and Dr. Wagner, Jr. had a brief run with the [[CMLL World Trios Championship]] as they won the title by defeating [[Black Warrior (wrestler)|Black Warrior]], Mr. Niebla and Antifaz del Norte and held them for 91 days before losing the belts to [[Atlantis (wrestler)|Atlantis]], Black Warrior and Mr. Niebla.<ref name=CMLLTrios/>

Following his year long stint in CMLL Fuerza Guerrera returned to AAA. At [[Triplemanía XIII]] teamed with Los Hell Brothers ([[Chessman (wrestler)|Chessman]] and [[Cibernético]]) in main event, losing to Latin Lover, [[La Parka (AAA)|La Parka]] and Fuerza's career long rival Octagón.<ref name="Trip13">{{cite web | url = http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/aaa/triple.html#xiii| title = Asistencia Asesoria y Administracion TripleMania | access-date = January 9, 2010| publisher=Pro Wrestling History}}</ref> In 2007 became involved in a storyline where he would actually wrestle his own son, Juventud Guerrera for the first time in his career. The two met in a [[Professional wrestling match types#Hardcore-based variations|Street Fight]] at [[Triplemanía XV]] which saw Juventud defeat his father.<ref name="Trip15">{{cite web | url = http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/aaa/triple.html#xv|title=Asistencia Asesoria y Administracion TripleMania | access-date = January 9, 2010|publisher=Pro Wrestling History}}</ref> Fuerza wrestled his last major match for AAA when he took part in a joint AAA/[[Pro Wrestling NOAH]] show, [[TripleSEM]] on September 3, 2007. Fuerza teamed with Antifaz and [[Histeria (wrestler)|Histeria]], losing to the Mexican Powers (Juventud, [[Joe Líder]] and [[Crazy Boy]]) in a match that also involved [[El Elegido]], [[Kenta Kobayashi|KENTA]] and [[Taiji Ishimori]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://superluchas.com/super-luchas-desde-japon-resultados-triplesem-en-el-differ-ariake-de-tokio-3-sep-07/|title=Súper Luchas desde Japón: Resultados TripleSEM en el Differ Ariake de Tokio (3 SEP 07)|date=September 3, 2007|author=Yoav|access-date=September 12, 2009|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|language=es}}</ref>

===International Wrestling Revolution Group (2008–present)===
In 2007 Fuerza Guerrera worked his final match for AAA and began working on the independent circuit and making regularly appearances for [[International Wrestling Revolution Group]] (IWRG). One of Guerrera's early IWRG appearances was at the 2008 ''Rey del Ring'' (Spanish for "King of the Ring") tournament, which was won by [[Scorpio, Jr.]]<ref name=Lucha2008>{{cite news|title=Lo Mejor de la Lucha Libre Mexicana 2008|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|id=296|date=January 6, 2008|url=http://superluchas.com/?p=11145|access-date=July 11, 2009|language=es}}</ref> On May 5, 2008, Fuerza Guerrera defeated [[Multifacético]] to win the [[IWRG Intercontinental Welterweight Championship]].<ref name=IWRGWelter/> Besides working for IWRG Fuerza Guerrera also worked on [[Blue Demon, Jr.]]'s NWA Mexico debut show, teaming with [[El Dandy]] and Hijo del Siltario in a main event loss to Blue Demon, Jr., [[El Hijo del Santo]] and [[Rayo de Jalisco, Jr.]]<ref name=Lucha2008/> On June 7, 2008, Guerrera lost the IWRG Welterweight title to Black Terry only to regain it on November 16, 2008.<ref name=IWRGWelter/> Guerrera still works for IWRG as well as helping his son build a new wrestling promotion called "Gran Prix Championship Wrestling Super-X" (GPCW). Despite not working for the same promotion both Octagón and Fuerza Guerrera have expressed a desire for a one on one ''Luchas de Apuesta'' between the two before either of them retire from wrestling. On May 23, 2010, Guerrera lost the IWRG Intercontinental Welterweight championship to [[Dr. Cerebro]] after holding the title for 553 days.

==Personal life==
Fuerza Guerrera's real name is not a matter of public record, as is often the case with [[wrestling mask|masked]] wrestlers in Mexico where their private lives are kept a secret from the wrestling fans.<ref name=Mondo>{{cite book|author=Madigan, Dan|title=Mondo Lucha a Go Go: the bizarre and honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling|publisher=HarperCollins Publishers|year=2007|chapter=Okay... what is Lucha Libre?|pages=29–40|isbn=978-0-06-085583-3}}</ref>

Fuerza Guerrera is the father of professional wrestler [[Juventud Guerrera]].<ref name=OWOWJuvi>{{cite web|url=http://www.onlineworldofwrestling.com/profiles/j/juventud-guerrera.html|title=Juventud Guerrera|publisher=Online World of Wrestling|access-date=January 5, 2010}}</ref> On October 9, 2018, Guerrera presented his other children as professional wrestlers, his son Fuerza Guerrera Jr/El Hijo de Fuerza Guerrera and his daughter Fuerza Guerrera/Hija de Fuerza Guerrera.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://solowrestling.mundodeportivo.com/new/75097-juventud-guerrera-acusa-de-fraude-a-fuerza-guerrera-y-sus-hermanos|title=Juventud Guerrera señala a los hijos de Fuerza Guerrera de luchar sin licencia|date=October 10, 2018|website=solowrestling.mundodeportivo.com |author1=Solowrestling }}</ref> He is also the uncle of professional wrestler Furia Guerrera, who after a brief stint in AAA in 1998 wrestled in the [[independent circuit]] until his murder in August 2009.

He is signed to [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL), where he is the leader of the ''[[Los Guerreros Laguneros]]'' [[Glossary of professional wrestling terms#Stable|stable]] and part of the CMLL [[Glossary of professional wrestling terms#Book|booking]] committee.{{cite web | url= http://www.f4wonline.com/component/content/article/20746/ | title= Tues update: Tons more on Savage, Kharma update, Punk/Bret, new WWE office, more | author=Alvarez, Bryan | author-link=Bryan Alvarez |date= May 24, 2011 | access-date= September 12, 2011 | work=[[Dave Meltzer#Wrestling Observer Newsletter|Wrestling Observer Newsletter]] | archive-date=September 10, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120910223110/http://www.f4wonline.com/component/content/article/20746/}} He also makes appearances for partner [[Promotion (wrestling)|promotion]] [[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]] (NJPW). Guerrero debuted in 1990 and joined CMLL in 1997, where he has held several titles, including the [[CMLL World Heavyweight Championship]] twice, the [[CMLL World Light Heavyweight Championship]] and [[NWA World Historic Middleweight Championship]] once, the [[CMLL World Trios Championship]] five times, and the [[CMLL World Tag Team Championship]] six times. He is a two-time [[CMLL Universal Championship]] tournament winner and three-time ''[[CMLL Torneo Gran Alternativa|Torneo Gran Alternativa]]'' winner, also winning the [[CMLL International Gran Prix]] twice and the ''[[Leyenda de Azul]]'' once. He has also wrestled for [[Impact Wrestling|Total Nonstop Action Wrestling]] (TNA) in the United States, where he won the [[2008 TNA World X Cup Tournament|2008 World X Cup]] as part of [[Team Mexico]], as well as [[Ring of Honor]] (ROH), [[All Elite Wrestling]] (AEW) and [[Major League Wrestling]] (MLW), where he won the [[MLW National Openweight Championship]]. Hernández is the older brother of [[Gran Guerrero]], who was initially billed as his storyline son. He is not related to the professional wrestling legend [[Gory Guerrero]] or any of his children; "Guerrero" in this case is the Spanish word for [[warrior]] and not the [[surname]] of the character. He wrestled under a [[Wrestling mask|mask]] for the majority of his career until losing it in a [[Lucha libre#Luchas de Apuestas|''Lucha de Apuestas'']] ("bet match") to [[Atlantis (wrestler)|Atlantis]] in September 2014, being forced to unmask and reveal his birth name. ==Professional wrestling career== ===Early career (1990–1997)=== Gutiérrez's father started bringing him to professional wrestling shows at the Torreón Bullring before he was a year old; his mother nurtured the interest by buying him wrestling toys, masks and small rings. At the age of 15, he began practicing [[amateur wrestling]] at the "Gimnasio El Ranchero" arena in Sacramento, [[Gómez Palacio, Durango|Gómez Palacio]], and was such a regular attendee that he was asked to fill in for an absentee opening match wrestler during a scheduled show. He wrestled that night without wrestling boots as "Cóndor Dorado" ("Golden Condor"), impressing trainer Toñito El Detector enough to be accepted as a student into his professional wrestling class. Despite only having one semester left, he dropped out of high school to focus fully on his wrestling pursuits, which brought him under the tutalege of Torreón fixtures Gran Markus, Asterión and Halcón Suriano at the Palacio de los Deportes.{{cite web |last1=Alcántara |first1=Faustino |title=Último Guerrero, el soldador que arriesgó todo por la gloria, incluida su máscara |url=https://es-us.noticias.yahoo.com/ultimo-guerrero-arriesgo-todo-gloria-incluida-mascara-155725736.html |website=Yahoo! Deportes |access-date=10 April 2026}}{{cite news | author = Rosas Plata | title = Último Guerrero, listo para la lucha de Máscaras - Cobaré vengenza! | url = http://itecor.v1.myvirtualpaper.com/11032009/2009031101/en/?page=19 | work =Ovaciones | publisher = Editorial Ovaciones, S. A. de C.V. | location = [[Mexico]], [[Mexican Federal District|D.F.]] | id = Número 21523 Año LXII | page = 19 | date = March 11, 2009 | access-date = March 29, 2009 | language = es | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090318011751/http://itecor.v1.myvirtualpaper.com/11032009/2009031101/en/?page=19 | archive-date=March 18, 2009|first=Arturo}} Shortly after his debut, he adopted the [[Glossary of professional wrestling terms#Gimmick|gimmick]] of "Flanagan", based on [[Héctor Suárez]]'s titular character, to match his friend and training partner [[Luciferno|Super Punk]]. After working as a [[tag team]] in Durango-based [[Independent circuit|local promotions]] for several years, they received their first break in ''[[Promo Azteca]]'' on the invitation of Super Punk's older brother [[Ephesto|Panterita del Ring]]; [[Fuerza Guerrera]] and [[Blue Panther]] offered the two lodging under a ring at a gym in [[Iztapalapa]] for two years. At the behest of ''Promo Azteca's'' co-owner, Ricardo Reyes, the duo changed their names in 1996, with Gutiérrez adopting the name "Último Guerrero" ("Last Warrior") and Super Punk becoming "Último Rebelde"; they started using a British [[Hooliganism|hooligan]]-inspired gimmick with visual cues from [[Road Warriors|The Road Warriors]]. In late 1997, the team was scheduled to lose their masks in a ''[[Lucha libre#Luchas de Apuestas|Lucha de Apuestas]]'' ("bet match"), however, Guerrero saved them by joining [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL).{{cite news | author = Enciclopedia staff | title = Grandes Figuras de la Lucha Libre | work = Último Guerrero | location = Portales, Mexico | id = 17 | page = 66 | date = November 2008 | language = es}} ===Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (1997–present)=== ==== Early years (1997–1999) ==== Upon his CMLL debut, Último Guerrero experienced moderate success working lower card matches, usually the first-to-third match on the show. At the [[CMLL 65th Anniversary Show]] on September 11, 1998, Guerrero defeated [[Mr. Águila]] in his first ''Lucha de Apuestas'' at CMLL's main arena, [[Arena México]], forcing his opponent to unmask and reveal his real name.{{cite news|title=1998 Especial!|work=Box y Lucha Magazine|pages=2–28|id=issue 2348|date=January 9, 1999|language=es}} In 1999, he and Blue Panther won the ''[[CMLL Torneo Gran Alternativa|Torneo Gran Alternativa]]'' ("Great Alternative Tournament"), in which a young wrestler teams with a veteran. On May 21, Guerrero unsuccessfully challenged [[The Great Sasuke]] for the [[NWA World Middleweight Championship]].{{cite news|title=1999 Especial!|work=Box y Lucha Magazine|pages=2–28|id=issue 2436|date=January 10, 2000|language=es}} ====''Los Infernales'' (1999–2001)==== {{main|Los Infernales}} In 1999, Guerrero and [[Rey Bucanero]] joined [[El Satánico]]'s reformed ''[[Los Infernales]]'' stable.{{cite news|title=Enciclopedia de las Mascaras|work=Rey Bucanero|location=[[Mexico]]|id=Tomo IV|page=11|date=October 2007|language=es}}{{cite news|title=Grandes Figuras de la Lucha Libre|work=Satánico|location=Portales, Mexico|id=17|page=55|date=November 2008|language=es}} In the summer of 2000, he and Bucanero last defeated [[Mr. Niebla]] and [[Villano IV]] in a sixteen-team tournament to win the vacant [[CMLL World Tag Team Championship]].{{cite web | url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/emll/ppv.html#0800 | title= August 2000 PPV "Entre Torre Infernal" | date= August 4, 2000 | access-date= February 23, 2010 | publisher= Pro Wrestling History}}{{cite web | url = http://wrestling-titles.com/mexico/emll/cmll-t.html |title = Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre Tag Team Title | access-date = March 4, 2009 |publisher = wrestling-titles.com}} During Satánico's [[Feud (professional wrestling)|storyline feud]] against [[Toscano (wrestler)|Tarzan Boy]], Guerrero and Bucanero [[Turn (professional wrestling)|turned]] on Satánico; each wrestler claimed that they deserved the name ''Los Infernales'' and Satánico was holding them back. In response, during a televised segment, Satánico recruited two other wrestlers to even the numbers, which was presented as if he used his "Satanic powers" to turn wrestler Rencor Latino into [[Averno (wrestler)|Averno]] ("Hell") and Astro Rey Jr. into [[Mephisto (wrestler)|Mephisto]]. When Tarzan Boy was injured and unable to wrestle, Guerrero and Bucanero recruited [[Máscara Mágica II|Máscara Mágica]] to even the numbers. The storyline between the two factions culminated when all seven wrestlers fought in a [[steel cage match]] at the [[CMLL 68th Anniversary Show]] on September 28, 2001, where the winning side would gain the rights to the ''Los Infernales'' name. In the end, Satánico pinned Mágica to gain the rights and his mask.{{Cite web |date=September 2, 2010 |title=Historia de los Aniversarios del CMLL |url=http://www.thegladiatores.com/?p=3072 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921062825/http://www.thegladiatores.com/?p=3072 |archive-date=September 21, 2013 |access-date=June 8, 2026 |website=The Gladiatores |language=es}} ====''Los Guerreros del Infierno'' (2001–2005)==== {{main|Los Guerreros del Infierno}} Guerrero, Bucanero and Tarzan Boy subsequently became known collectively as ''[[Los Guerreros del Infierno]]'' ("The Infernal Soldiers").{{cite news|title=Rey Bucanero: tradición y el honor |work=[[Súper Luchas]]|id=Issue 82|date=November 3, 2004|language=es}} After a match with an inconclusive finish in October, Guerrero and Bucanero lost the CMLL World Tag Team Championship to [[El Hijo del Santo]] and [[Negro Casas]] on November 2, but regained it on May 31, 2002.{{cite news|title=2002: considerar detrás|work=Box y Lucha Magazine|id=2593|date=January 19, 2003|language=es}} ''Los Guerreros del Infierno'' then began feuding with [[Shocker (wrestler)|Shocker]] and [[Vampiro|Vampiro Canadiense]], whom they successfully defended the title against at the [[CMLL 69th Anniversary Show]] on September 13. On December 13, at [[Sin Piedad (2002)|''Sin Piedad'']] ("No Mercy"), Guerrero defeated Shocker to win the [[CMLL World Light Heavyweight Championship]], his first singles title in CMLL.{{cite web | url=https://superluchas.com/video-del-recuerdo-lo-mejor-de-sin-piedad-2003-vampiro-rapa-a-bucanero-ultimo-guerreo-gana-campeonato-a-shocker/ | title=Video del recuerdo: Lo mejor de "Sin Piedad 2002" Vampiro rapa a Bucanero, Último Guerreo gana campeonato a Shocker | first=Alex | last=Ruiz Glez | date=December 8, 2012 | access-date=December 9, 2012 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] | language=es}} ''Los Guerreros'' lost and regained the title from [[L. A. Park|L.A. Par-K]] and Shocker in early 2004,{{cite news|title=Número Especial – Lo mejor de la lucha libre mexicana durante el 2004|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|id=91|date=January 24, 2005|language=es}} but Bucanero suffered a knee injury and was temporarily replaced by [[Black Warrior (wrestler)|Black Warrior]]; they lost the title to [[Atlantis (wrestler)|Atlantis]] and Blue Panther on June 25. In early 2005, Guerrero began a feud with [[Místico]], sparking a tag program pitting him and Bucanero against Místico and [[Dr. Wagner Jr.]]{{cite news|title=2005 Lo Mejor de la Lucha Mexicana|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|id=140|date=January 3, 2006|language=es}} ====''Los Guerreros de la Atlantida'' (2005–2011)==== {{main|Los Guerreros del Infierno|l1=Los Guerreros de la Atlantida}} [[File:U-Guerrero.jpg|thumb|Último Guerrero in December 2010]] In late 2005, Guerrero aligned with the now-''[[Heel (professional wrestling)|rudo]]'' Atlantis, and ''Los Guerreros'' was renamed ''Los Guerreros de la Atlantida'' ("The Warriors of the Atlantis").{{cite news | author = Enciclopedia staff | title = Grandes Figuras de la Lucha Libre | work = Atlantis | location = Portales, Mexico | id = 17 | page = 8 | date = November 2008 | language = es}} He and Tarzan Boy eventually ejected Bucanero from the group, tearing up his tights. On July 14, 2006, Bucanero defeated Guerrero for the CMLL World Light Heavyweight Championship, ending his three-and-a-half year reign.{{cite news|title=Lo Mejor de la Lucha Libre Mexicana duranted el 2006|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|id=Issue 192|date=December 23, 2006|url=http://Superluchas.com/super-luchas-193/|access-date=July 11, 2009|language=es}} On July 13, 2007, Guerrero and Dr. Wagner Jr. defeated Casas and Místico for the CMLL World Tag Team Championship, but lost it in a rematch the following week, marking the shortest reign in the title's history. On July 18, 2008, he and [[Dragón Rojo Jr.]] defeated [[Alberto Del Rio|Dos Caras Jr.]] and [[Gran Metalik|Metalik]] in the finals of that year's ''[[Torneo Gran Alternativa (2008)|Torneo Gran Alternativa]]''. On August 5, Guerrero, Atlantis and Casas defeated [[Santos Escobar|El Hijo del Fantasma]], [[Héctor Garza]] and [[La Máscara]] for the [[CMLL World Trios Championship]],{{Cite news |last=Rosas Plata |first=Arturo |date=August 5, 2008 |title=Garza y sus Ángeles, por una defensa mas |work=Ovaciones |page=16 |language=es}} which they successfully defended against [[Alex Shelley]], [[Chris Sabin]] and [[Sonjay Dutt]] at the [[CMLL 75th Anniversary Show]] on September 19.{{Cite news |last=Rosas Plata |first=Arturo |date=September 20, 2008 |title=Acabó con la leyenda de Panther |work=Ovaciones |page=21 |language=es}} On December 22, Guerrero defeated Dos Caras Jr. to win his first [[CMLL World Heavyweight Championship]]. He used this to provide for himself when he first arrived in [[Mexico City]] in 1995, constructing animal cages for a veterinary supply factory in [[La Merced (neighborhood)|La Merced]] that [[Fuerza Guerrera]] had secured him employment at. It also helped him secure his spot in [[Promo Azteca]], where he was put in charge of building, assembling and dismantling the lighting rigs. Many sources mistakenly list [[Hooligan (wrestler)|Hooligan]] and [[Ephesto]] as brothers of José Gutiérrez, but they are not blood relatives. Gutiérrez, Ephesto and Hooligan trained together and became close friends, often referring to each other as "brother" without having any blood relationship. Hooligan and Ephesto are brothers, which is why Ephesto is sometimes mistaken for Gutiérrez's brother as well.{{cite book | author= Madigan, Dan | title= Mondo Lucha Libre: the bizarre & honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling | publisher= HarperCollins Publishers | year= 2007 | chapter = A family affair | pages = 128–132 | isbn=978-0-06-085583-3}} In 2008, Último Guerrero introduced "Último Guerrero Jr." to the wrestling world. While it is not uncommon for fake relatives to be promoted in ''lucha libre'', it is believed that Último Guerrero Jr. is indeed the son of Último Guerrero. Later on, Guerrero Jr. would be reintroduced as [[Gran Guerrero]], with the storyline explanation being that Gran Guerrero was the much younger brother of Último Guerrero. On May 19, 2017, footage emerged of Daniel Alvarado ([[Brazo de Platino]]) and other members of the [[Alvarado wrestling family|Alvarado family]], notably his nephews José ([[Máximo Sexy]]), Felipe Alvarado ([[La Máscara (wrestler)|La Máscara]]), [[Psycho Clown]] and [[Robin (wrestler)|Robin]], destroying a [[Ford Mustang]] belonging to Gutiérrez.{{cite web | url=http://www.mediotiempo.com/lucha-libre/2017/05/19/familia-alvarado-destrozo-automovil-de-ultimo-guerrero | title=Familia Alvarado destrozó automóvil de Último Guerrero | date=May 19, 2017 | access-date=May 20, 2017 | work=MedioTiempo | publisher=[[MSN]] | language=es}}{{cite web | url=http://www.record.com.mx/mas-deportes-lucha/maximo-habria-destruido-auto-de-ultimo-guerrero | work=[[Récord (Mexican newspaper)|Récord]] | language=es | date=May 19, 2017 | access-date=May 20, 2017 | title=Máximo habría destruido auto de Último Guerrera}} The vandalism was reportedly motivated by the fact that Gutiérrez had spoken out against Felipe Alvarado as a possible head of the wrestlers' union after the death of Alvarado's father. The head of the CMLL wrestlers' union had been in the Alvarado family for over a decade, and the Alvarado family believed it should go to someone in their family.{{cite web | url=https://superluchas.com/motivo-del-ataque-los-alvarado-al-automovil-ultimo-guerrero/ | title=Motivo del ataque de los Alvarado al automóvil de Último Guerrero | first=Carlos | last=Acosta | date=May 19, 2017 | access-date=May 20, 2017 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] | language=es | editor-first=Ernesto | editor-last=Ocampo }} The following day, CMLL reportedly fired both Felipe and José Alvarado.{{cite web | url= https://superluchas.com/maximo-la-mascara-del-cmll-sindicato-luchadores-nido-corrupcion/ | title=Máximo y La Máscara fuera del CMLL — El Sindicato de Luchadores, nido de corrupción | first=Ernesto | last=Ocampo | date=May 20, 2017 | access-date=May 20, 2017 | work=[[Súper Luchas]] | language=es }} He is married to [[Lluvia]], and is the step-father to her daughter Tabata.{{cite web |title=early week CMLL results, all women's show lineup, |url=https://thecubsfan.com/cmll/2025/10/15/early-week-cmll-results-all-womens-show-lineup/ |access-date=14 December 2025}} He also has at least two daughters named Sheila{{cite web |title=La hija del Último Guerrero |url=https://x.com/PuroLibre/status/865716824712892416 |website=Twitter |access-date=30 May 2026}} and Paola, and a son with Lluvia born circa-2017.{{cite web |title=In the ring, they were gods. '''Genaro Vázquez Nevarez''' (born September 18, 1960) is a Mexican [[professional wrestler]] and trainer, best known under his [[ring name]] '''Blue Panther'''. He made his in-ring debut in 1978. Since then, he has worked for most major Mexican [[professional wrestling promotion]]s, including the [[Universal Wrestling Association]] (UWA), [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL) and [[Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide|Asistencia, Asesoría y Administración]] (AAA). He was one of the first wrestlers to leave CMLL for AAA when it was created in 1992, but returned to CMLL in 1997, where he has competed ever since.

Vázquez's two oldest sons, known as [[Blue Panther Jr.]] and [[Black Panther (wrestler)|Black Panther]], are also professional wrestlers, working for CMLL since 2013. A third son referred to as El Hijo de Blue Panther also wrestles. He was the first [[CMLL World Middleweight Championship|CMLL World Middleweight Champion]] and has won the [[Mexican National Middleweight Championship]] twice, the [[CMLL World Trios Championship]] twice, and the [[Mexican National Trios Championship]]. He also won the 1999 ''[[CMLL Torneo Gran Alternativa|Torneo Gran Alternativa]]'' and the 2000 ''[[Leyenda de Plata]]'' tournaments. Blue Panther has also wrestled in the United States for [[Major League Wrestling]] (MLW), where he won the [[MLW National Openweight Championship]], and [[Ring of Honor]] (ROH).

In his career, he has won the [[wrestling mask|masks]] of such notable wrestlers as [[Black Man (wrestler)|Black Man]], [[Lizmark Jr.]] and [[Art Barr|Love Machine]]. In 2008, he lost his own mask to [[Villano V]], and has since had his hair shaved off as a result of losses to [[Averno (wrestler)|Averno]] and [[Sam Adonis]]. Vázquez opened his own gym in the early 1990s, where he was one of the first Mexican professional wrestling trainers to train both men and women.

==Professional wrestling career==
===Early career (1978–1981)===
Blue Panther began wrestling in northern [[Mexico]] in the late 1970s before getting noticed by wrestler and promoter [[René Guajardo]] in [[Monterrey]].<ref name=FelizSL/> During his initial years in Monterrey, he was given several opportunities to show off his in-ring skills and work higher profile matches, in particular with ''[[Lucha de Apuestas]]'' ("bet match") wins, where he defeated and unmasked La Bestia, Simio Blanco and Oro.{{efn|name=Matematico}}{{efn|name=OroApuesta}}

===Universal Wrestling Association (1981–1990)===
Guarjardo got Blue Panther booked in the [[Universal Wrestling Association]] (UWA), and in 1981, he made his debut in their main venue, the ''El Toreo de Cuatro Caminos'' bullfighting arena in [[Naucalpan]]. After wrestling on the undercard as a ''[[heel (professional wrestling)|rudo]]'' (also referred to as a "heel", those that portray the "bad guys" in wrestling), he received his first [[push (professional wrestling)|push]] in 1984, winning the [[UWA World Welterweight Championship]] from veteran worker Matemático.<ref name=UWAWelter/><ref name="DiaDec16">{{cite web | url=https://superluchas.com/en-un-dia-como-hoy-carnaval-de-campeones-en-el-toreo/ | title=En un día como hoy... Carnaval de Campeones en El Toreo |trans-title=On a day like today... Carnival of Champions in El Toreo | first=Teddy | last=Centinela | work=[[Súper Luchas]] | date=December 16, 2014 | language=es|access-date=June 5, 2026}}</ref> Panther also began teaming with [[Black Man (wrestler)|Black Man]] on a regular basis around that time, including a November 20 ''Lucha de Apuestas'' win over ''Los Sombras de Plata'', forcing both members of the team to unmask.<ref name="EncyBlackMan" /> The team later broke up, leading to a prolonged storyline feud between the two, which included Black Man winning the UWA World Welterweight Championship from Blue Panther on February 9, 1986.<ref name="UWAWelter" /> The storyline built to a high-profile ''Lucha de Apuestas'' between the two at the ''El Toreon Cuatro Caminos''. After three long falls, Blue Panther defeated Black Man, forcing him to unmask and state his real name, per ''[[lucha libre]]'' traditions.<ref name="EncyBlackMan" />

On November 16, Blue Panther defeated [[Gran Hamada]] to win his first [[UWA World Junior Light Heavyweight Championship]].<ref name="UWAJLh" /> His first reign, which lasted 190 days, was ended by [[El Solar]] on May 25, 1987. He later regained the championship on February 8, 1988.<ref name="UWAJLh" /> In May, Blue Panther won another significant match, unmasking [[Kendo (wrestler)|Kendo]] in [[Tijuana|Tijuana, Baja California]].<ref name="EncyKendo" /> On September 18, Blue Panther's second and final reign as the UWA World Junior Light Heavyweight Champion ended as the UWA bookers decided to have [[Gran Cochisse]] win the championship from him.<ref name="UWAJLh" />

===Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (1991–1992)===
In 1991, Panther began working full-time for [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre|Empresa Mexicana de Lucha Libre]] (EMLL) as a top ''rudo''. He began a feud with [[Atlantis (wrestler)|Atlantis]] over the [[NWA World Middleweight Championship]], but was unsuccessful in his August title challenge.{{efn|''Blue Panther 30 Años'' (2008) p. 14 "Empresa Mexicana de Lucha Libre"{{sfn|L2K Staff|p=14}}}} Later that year, EMLL changed their name to Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL; "World Wrestling Council") and held tournaments for CMLL-branded championships. Blue Panther was one of sixteen competitors entered in the tournament for the [[CMLL World Middleweight Championship]], defeating [[Ringo Mendoza]] in the opening round, [[El Dandy]] in the semi-finals and [[El Satánico]] in the finals to become the inaugural champion.<ref name=CMLLMiddle/> 

Following his victory, Blue Panther was programmed in a feud with [[Art Barr|American Love Machine]], elevating his status as one of the top stars of ''lucha libre'' at the time. The storyline built to the main event of ''[[Aniversario de Arena México#36. Aniversario de Arena México|36. Aniversario de Arena México]]'' on April 3, 1992, at [[Arena México]], where the event drew a sold-out crowd of 18,000, prompting CMLL to use closed-circuit screens for an additional 8,000 spectators. In the third and deciding fall, Love Machine used a move called ''[[piledriver (professional wrestling)#Belly to belly piledriver|El Martinete']]'' (a "piledriver") which, under ''lucha libre'' rules, caused him to be disqualified and lose the match; per storyline, Love Machine was not aware of the specific rule, unique to Mexico, and thus was "robbed" of the victory. After the loss, Love Machine reluctantly unmasked and revealed his real name, Art Barr.{{efn|''Blue Panther 30 Años'' (2008) p. 16 "Contra Love Machine Art Barr"{{sfn|L2K Staff|p=16}}}}<ref name=ArtBarr>{{cite web|url=http://slam.canoe.com/WrestlingStarBios/barr_art.html|title=Art Barr: What could have been; Looking back at Love Machine's career|last=Molinaro|first=John|access-date=October 12, 2008|work=Slam! Sports|publisher=[[Canadian Online Explorer]]|archive-date=June 24, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150624042734/http://slam.canoe.com/WrestlingStarBios/barr_art.html}}</ref>

===Asistencia, Asesoría y Administración (1992–1997)===
[[File:Blue-Panther.jpg|thumb|left|Blue Panther wearing his signature mask.]]

In mid-1992, then-CMLL-[[Booker (professional wrestling)|booker]] [[Antonio Peña]] left CMLL over creative differences with the owner and formed his own company, [[Asistencia, Asesoría y Administración]] (AAA).{{efn|''Blue Panther 30 Años'' (2008) p. 17 "Triple A"{{sfn|L2K Staff|p=17}}}} Panther, who was close to Peña, left CMLL to join AAA, resulting in the CMLL World Middleweight Championship being declared vacant.<ref name=CMLLMiddle/> On July 23, Blue Panther won the [[Mexican National Middleweight Championship]] from [[Octagón]], holding the title for 665 days until Octagón regained the championship on April 30, 1994.<ref name="MexMiddleBook" /><ref name="MexMiddleMag" /> In July 1993, Blue Panther faced Love Machine, who joined AAA months after him, in a mask vs. hair match, during which both wrestlers changed sides. Love Machine was helped by [[Eddie Guerrero|Eddy Guerrero]], turning ''rudo'', while Blue Panther became a ''[[Face (professional wrestling)|tecnico]]'' (a "face", those that portray the "good guys" in wrestling) as he "valiantly" fought back and defeated Love Machine.{{efn|name=ArtHair}} Afterwards, Barr and Guerrero formed [[Los Gringos Locos]]'','''which soon became the main ''rudo'' group of AAA''.{{efn|name=ArtHair}}''

Blue Panther's second reign as Mexican National Middleweight Champion lasted a total of 609 days, from May 27, 1994 to January 26, 1996, when [[El Hijo del Santo]] won the championship.<ref name=MexMiddleBook/><ref name=MexMiddleMag/> On November 6, 1994, Blue Panther, [[Jerry Estrada]] and [[L. A. Park|La Parka]] lost to [[2 Cold Scorpio]], [[Chris Benoit]] and [[Tito Santana]] at [[AAA When Worlds Collide]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 6, 2013 |title=Nov. 6 in history: "When Worlds Collide" - Mysterio, Guerrero, Konnan, Benoit featured on AAA/WCW PPV event |url=https://www.pwtorch.com/artman2/publish/Torch_Today_2/article_74386.shtml |access-date=June 5, 2026 |website=Pro Wrestling Torch}}</ref> On July 6, 1995, Panther, [[Fuerza Guerrera]] and [[Psicosis]] defeated Octagón, [[Rey Mysterio|Rey Misterio Jr.]] and [[Super Muñeco]] to win the [[Mexican National Trios Championship]].<ref name=MexTag/> After the [[1994 economic crisis in Mexico|downturn of the Mexican economy]], Blue Panther and Guerrera started their own promotion called ''Promotora Mexicana de Lucha Libre ''(PROMELL; later known as ''[[Promo Azteca]]''). The Mexico City Boxing and Professional wrestling commission took control of the Mexican National Trios Championship away from AAA and awarded it to PROMELL instead, leading to the championship being vacated in 1996, before Panther won it again with Guerrera and [[El Signo]] by defeating [[El Brazo]], [[Súper Brazo]] and Super Elektra.<ref name="MexTag" /> As the original PROMELL struggled to be profitable, Blue Panther briefly returned to AAA in 1997.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=1458&view=&page=4&gimmick=&year=1997&promotion=&region=&location=&arena=&showtype=&constellationType=&worker= | title=Blue Panther >> Matches >> 1997 | access-date=March 10, 2019 | work=CageMatch}}</ref>

===Return to CMLL (1997–present)===
In 1998, Panther teamed with [[Dr. Wagner Jr.]] and his real-life nephew [[Black Warrior (wrestler)|Black Warrior]] to form "Los Laguneros", defeating [[Bestia Salvaje]], [[Scorpio Jr.]] and [[Zumbido]] in a tournament final on December 18 to win the vacant [[CMLL World Trios Championship]].<ref name="CMLL3" /> In April 1999, Panther and [[Último Guerrero]] won that year's [[Torneo Gran Alternativa (April 1999)|''Torneo Gran Alternativa'']] ("Great Alternative Tournament").<ref name=Ganador/> The trios championship was vacated in 2002 after Black Warrior left ''Los Laguneros''. Guerrera replaced Black Warrior on the team, which won another tournament for it; they reigned for only three months before dropping the titles to Black Warrior, [[Atlantis (wrestler)|Atlantis]] and [[Mr. Niebla]]. Blue Panther soon transitioned into a ''técnico'' and began teaming with Atlantis, [[Lizmark Jr.]] and Mr. Niebla as ''La Ola Azul'' ("The Blue Wave"), feuding with ''[[Los Guerreros del Infierno]]''. In 2004, Atlantis and Blue Panther defeated Guerrero and [[Rey Bucanero]] to win the [[CMLL World Tag Team Championship]], which they held until losing it to [[Averno (wrestler)|Averno]] and [[Mephisto (wrestler)|Mephisto]] in April 2005. When Atlantis turned ''rudo'', Panther feuded with him intermittently, and the two often ripped at each other's [[wrestling mask|masks]], hinting at a possible mask vs. mask match. At the [[CMLL 75th Anniversary Show]] on September 19, 2008, Blue Panther lost his mask to [[Villano V]], thus forcing him to state his birth name, Genaro Vázquez Nevarez.<ref name="CMLL75SL" /><ref name="CMLL75Ovaciones" />

In late 2011, Blue Panther began feuding with ''[[La Peste Negra]]'' ("The Black Plague"; [[Negro Casas]] and [[El Felino]]), leading to a hair vs. hair match between him and El Felino in the main event of ''[[Sin Piedad (2011)|Sin Piedad]]'' ("No Mercy") on December 16. A week prior to the match, Panther was disqualified in a tag team match after giving El Felino a piledriver. This led to the Distrito Federal Box y Lucha Commission announcing that Panther was suspended for two weeks, starting after the event,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://superluchas.com/video-blue-panther-si-podra-luchar-el-proximo-viernes-en-sin-piedad/|title=Video: Blue Panther sí podrá luchar el próximo viernes en "Sin Piedad" | trans-title=Video: Blue Panther will be able to fight next Friday a "Sin Piedad"|last=Ruiz Glez|first=Alex|date=December 15, 2011|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|access-date=December 19, 2011|language=es}}</ref> where El Felino was disqualified after the referee caught him going for a piledriver; as a result, El Felino was shaved bald.<ref name="SinPiedad2011">{{cite web|url=https://superluchas.com/blue-panther-gana-la-cabellera-del-felino-via-descalificacion/|title=Blue Panther gana la cabellera del Felino vía descalificación | trans-title=Blue Panther wins the hair of El Felino via disqualification |last=Ruiz Glez|first=Alex|date=December 17, 2011|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|access-date=December 17, 2011|language=es}}</ref> On March 2, 2012, at ''[[Homenaje a Dos Leyendas (2012)|Homenaje a Dos Leyendas]]'' ("Homage to Two Legends"), Panther and Casas wrestled to a draw in a ''Lucha de Apuestas'' and were both shaved bald.<ref name="Leyendas2012">{{cite web|url=http://www.mediotiempo.com/lucha-libre/cmll/blue-panther-y-negro-casas-rapados|title=Blue Panther y Negro Casas rapados | trans-title=Blue Panther and Negro Casas shaved|author=Valdés, Apolo|date=March 3, 2012|access-date=March 3, 2012|work=Medio Tiempo|publisher=[[MSN]]|language=es}}</ref> In March 2013, Blue Panther was forced to team up with ''rudo'' [[Rey Escorpión]] in the 2013 ''[[CMLL Torneo Nacional de Parejas Increibles (2013)|Torneo Nacional de Parejas Increibles]]'' ("National Incredible Pairs Tournament"), a tournament where a ''rudo'' and ''tecnico'' team up. ==Professional wrestling style==
Over the years, Vázquez has become known for his "Ras de Lona" ("On the mat") wrestling style, focusing more on holds, takedowns and submission moves than high flying wrestling. The style is personified by his ''Nudo Lagunero'' ("The Lagunero Knot") submission move that he created. The "Nudo Lagunero" is a [[Professional wrestling holds#Standing figure-four leglock|standing figure-four leglock]], where Vázquez first wraps a prone opponent's legs across each other, then stretches the opponent's arms through the "knot" of the legs and pulls them up in the air so that all pressure is on the arms to force a submission.<ref name=PWI500-2008>{{cite news|title=Pro Wrestling Illustrated 500 – 2008: 313 Blue Panther|work=[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]|publisher=Sports and Entertainment publications LLC|location=Blue Bell, [[Pennsylvania]], United States|id=October 2008|page=112|date=August 2008}}</ref> In addition to the more complicated ''Nudo'', he also uses the [[Fujiwara armbar]] submission hold, where Vázquez takes a face-down opponent's arm and pulls it back while laying on their back to put the pressure on the shoulder and elbow joints.<ref name=PWI500-2008/> While he is mostly known for his mat style, he will, on occasion, execute a dive out of the ring, such as a ''[[Professional wrestling aerial techniques#Suicide|Topé Suicida]]'', where he dives head first through the ropes to hit an opponent.<ref name=PWI500-2008/>

==Personal life==
Genaro Vázquez Nevarez was born on September 18, 1960,<ref name=FelizSL/> in the "Lagunero" town in Gómez Palacio, Durango, Mexico.<ref name="Almanac2008Stats"/> His oldest son was born in the mid-to-late 1980s, known professionally as "Blue Panther Jr.". His second son, known under the ring name "Black Panther", was born in either 1988 or 1989. A third son was introduced in mid-2018 under the ring name "El Hijo de Blue Panther". Vázquez is the uncle of Jesus Toral Lopez, better known as the professional wrestler Black Warrior,<ref name="MondoFamily">{{cite book|author=Madigan, Dan|title=Mondo Lucha A Go-Go: the bizarre & honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling|chapter=A Family Affair|pages=224–228|publisher=HarperCollins |year=2007|isbn=978-0-06-085583-3}}</ref> and the great-uncle of Toral's son [[Warrior Jr.]]<ref name=IWRGTag31>{{cite web | url=http://www.thegladiatores.com/eterno-gana-la-cabellera-de-bombero-infernal/ | title=Eterno gana la cabellera de Bombero Infernal. | trans-title=Eterno wins the hair of Bombero Infernal | date=September 4, 2017 | access-date=September 19, 2017 | work=The Gladiatores | language=es | first=Alfonso | last=Lizárraga}}</ref> Vázquez owns and operates his own [[chiropractic]] clinic, where he has treated several of his fellow wrestlers, as well as patients in general.<ref>{{cite web | work=The Gladiatores | language=es | access-date=March 15, 2019 | date=March 14, 2019 | url=http://www.thegladiatores.com/detras-de-la-lucha-blue-panther/| trans-title=Behind the Fight – Blue Panther | title=Detras de la lucha – Blue Panther | first=Alfonso | last=Lizarraga}}</ref>

{{short description|Mexican professional wrestler and actor}} {{about|the wrestler|the TV series|Blue Demon (TV series)|the 2004 film|Blue Demon (film)}} {{missing information|more detail on the person's life, and career|date=April 2018}} {{Use mdy dates|date=February 2019}} {{Infobox person | name = Blue Demon | birth_name = Alejandro Muñoz Moreno | image = Luchador Blue Demon en Blue Demon y las invasoras (1969).jpg | caption = Blue Demon in ''Blue Demon y las invasoras'' (1969) | birth_date = {{birth date|1922|10|12}} | birth_place = [[García, Nuevo León]], Mexico | children = [[Blue Demon Jr.]] (adopted) | spouse = Gregoria Moreno | death_date = {{death date and age|2000|12|16|1922|4|24}} | death_place = [[Mexico City]], Mexico | burial_place = Parque Memorial Gayosso
[[Naucalpan|Naucalpan de Juárez]] | module = {{Infobox professional wrestler | child=yes | ring_names = {{Unbulleted list|Tosco Muñoz|Blue Demon ("Demonio Azul"){{cite web|url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=3217|title=Blue Demon|access-date=August 11, 2017|work=Cagematch.net}}}} | height = {{convert|1.69|m|ftin|0|abbr=on}} | weight = {{convert|77|kg|lb|abbr=on}} | trainer = [[Rolando Vera (wrestler)|Rolando Vera]] | debut = March 31, 1948 | retired = August 27, 1989 }} }} '''Alejandro Muñoz Moreno''' (October 12, 1922 – December 16, 2000), better known by the [[ring name]] '''Blue Demon''' (''Demonio Azul'' in [[Spanish language|Spanish]]), was a Mexican film [[actor]] and [[professional wrestler]]. Blue Demon is considered a legend of [[professional wrestling in Mexico]], partially from starring in a series of ''[[Lucha films]]'' between 1961 and 1979, often alongside in-ring rival [[El Santo]]. His in-ring career began in 1948 and stretched for 41 years until his retirement in 1989. Throughout his career Muñoz never lost a ''[[Lucha de Apuestas]]'' match and retired without exposing his face to the public; he would later be buried in his signature blue and silver mask. In his 41-year career he won the [[NWA World Welterweight Championship]] twice, the [[Mexican National Welterweight Championship]] three times and the [[Mexican National Tag Team Championship]] with long time tag team partner [[Black Shadow (wrestler)|Black Shadow]]. He also won the hair of [[Cavernario Galindo]] and the masks of Espectro II, Matemático, and most notably, the mask of [[Rayo de Jalisco Sr.|Rayo de Jalisco]]. Near the end of his career Muñoz introduced [[Blue Demon Jr.]] to the wrestling world, who despite being promoted as the son of Blue Demon, did not actually share a blood connection to Muñoz; he was later claimed to be the "adopted son". Muñoz's actual son owns the trademarks to the name "Blue Demon", while Blue Demon Jr. owns the trademark to the "Blue Demon Jr." name. [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL) honors the legacy of Blue Demon by holding the ''[[Leyenda de Azul]]'' ("The Blue Legend") tournament at irregular intervals. He was chosen for the [[Wrestling Observer Newsletter Hall of Fame]] by Dave Meltzer in 1996 as part of the inaugural HOF selection. ==Early life== {{Professional wrestling sidebar}}Alejandro Muñoz Moreno was born October 12, 1922, in [[García, Nuevo León]], Mexico.{{cite book | author= Madigan, Dan | title= Mondo Lucha a Go Go: the bizarre& honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling | publisher= HarperCollins Publishers | year= 2007 | chapter = Los Enmascarados (the masked men): El Demonio Azul (the Blue Demon) | pages = 79–90| isbn=978-0-06-085583-3}} He was the child of farmers and was the fifth of twelve children. At a young age, Alejandro dropped out of school and moved to [[Monterrey]], where his uncle gave him a job working on the [[Ferrocarriles Nacionales de México|National Railroad]]. His co-workers gave him the nickname 'Manotas', referring to his large, powerful hands.{{cite book|author=Harris M. Lentz III|title=Obituaries in the Performing Arts, 2000: Film, Television, Radio, Theatre, Dance, Music, Cartoons and Pop Culture|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9XjGCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA28|date=June 1, 2001|publisher=McFarland|isbn=978-0-7864-1024-8|pages=28}} ==Professional wrestling career== A chance meeting with the famous Mexican wrestler [[Rolando Vera (wrestler)|Rolando Vera]] piqued his interest in [[Lucha Libre]], Vera even offering to tutor him and help him start a career. He began wrestling without a mask in [[Laredo, Texas]]. His first match was against Chema Lopez on March 12, 1948. Adopting the mask and persona of The Blue Demon, he headed back to Mexico to start a full-time in-ring career. His first appearance as The Blue Demon was in [[Mexico City]] in September 1948, where he fought Benny Arcilla. Blue Demon began his career in the ring as a [[Heel (professional wrestling)|rudo]] (a bad guy).{{cite book | author= Various | title= Lucha Libre: Masked Superstars of Mexican Wrestling | publisher= Distributed Art Publishers, Inc. | year= 2005 | chapter = El Demonio Azul / Blue Demon | pages = 162–186| isbn=968-6842-48-9}} {{cite news | author = L.L. Staff | title = Lucha Libre: Conoce la historia de las leyendas de cuadrilátero | work = Blue Demon (1922 - 2000) | location = [[Mexico]] | id = Grandes Figuras de la Lucha Libre | page = 11 | year = 2008|language = es}} From there, he formed a tag team with another masked [[Lucha libre|luchador]] named The Black Shadow, and the two became known as ''Los Hermanos Shadow'' (The Shadow Brothers). In 1952, the famous wrestler [[El Santo]] beat and unmasked [[Black Shadow (wrestler)|Black Shadow]] in the ring, which triggered Blue's decision to become a [[Face (professional wrestling)|técnico]] (a good guy) in the ring, and a legendary feud between Blue Demon and El Santo was started. The storyline feud between the two culminated with Blue Demon defeating El Santo in a well-publicized series of matches in 1952 and 1953. In 1953, Blue won the [[NWA World Welterweight Championship]] from Santo, and held it until 1958. Their rivalry never entirely abated in later years (although they co-starred in a number of Mexican horror films) since Santo always remembered his defeat at the Blue Demon's hands. During the 1960s, one of Blue Demon's rivals was el Rayo de Jalisco. In 1988, the year he retired, Blue Demon defeated Jalisco in a [[Professional wrestling match types#Luchas de apuestas|mask vs. mask match]], taking the mask of another of Mexico's wrestling legends.John F. Molinaro, ''The Top 100 Pro Wrestlers of All Time'', (Winding Stair Press: 2002), page 195.{{cite news | author = Enciclopedia staff | title = Enciclopedia de las Mascaras | work = Rayo de Jalisco | location = [[Mexico]] | id = Tomo IV | page = 6 | date = October 2007| language = es}} Blue Demon retired from the ring in 1989, aged 67, at the [[Monterrey Arena]], where he appeared in a final match, teaming up with his adoptive son, [[Blue Demon Jr.]] ==Acting career== Blue Demon first appeared in cameos in a couple of [[lucha film|luchador films]] released in 1961–1962, "The Killers of Lucha Libre" and "Fury in the Ring", in which he was one of several wrestlers more or less in the background. But in 1964, Enrique Vergara, the producer of the then-successful Santo movies, decided to diversify by allowing the 42-year-old Blue Demon to star in a series of luchador films of his own. The plots of the Blue Demon films are thought to be extremely similar to those of Santo's films. Santo was asking for a salary increase at the time and Vergara wanted to cultivate a second movie star.{{cite book|author=Robert Cotter|title=The Mexican Masked Wrestler and Monster Filmography|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C7rwCQAAQBAJ&pg=PA96|date=April 21, 2008|publisher=McFarland|isbn=978-1-4766-0419-0|pages=96}}{{cite book|author=Doyle Greene|title=Mexploitation Cinema: A Critical History of Mexican Vampire, Wrestler, Ape-Man and Similar Films, 1957–1977|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ci1zBgAAQBAJ&pg=PA86|date=May 29, 2012|publisher=McFarland|isbn=978-1-4766-0072-7|pages=85–86}} From 1964 to 1979, Blue Demon starred in a total of 25 action/horror/science fiction films. Of those 25 films, Santo co-starred with him in nine of them. In three of his films, Blue Demon starred as the leader of a squadron of masked superheroes known as ''Los Campeones Justicieros'' (The Champions of Justice). Membership in the Champions included such legendary Mexican wrestling figures as Blue Demon, [[Mil Máscaras]], [[Tinieblas]], [[Rayo de Jalisco]], [[El Médico Asesino]], El Fantasma Blanco, El Avispon Escarlata and Superzan. In 1989, Blue Demon was the subject of a feature-length Mexican documentary entitled ''Blue Demon, the Champion'' (1989). ==Death== Muñoz died just before noon on Saturday, December 16, 2000.{{cite web|url=http://www.canoe.com/SlamWrestlingInternational/mexico_timeline-can.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20021117013853/http://www.canoe.com/SlamWrestlingInternational/mexico_timeline-can.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 17, 2002|title=SLAM! Wrestling International -- 2000: The Year-In-Review Mexico|access-date=August 11, 2017|work=[[Canoe.com]]}} He suffered a fatal [[myocardial infarction|heart attack]] on a park bench near a subway kiosk while on his way home from his regular morning training session at The ''Blue Demon Instituto Atletico'', where he was teaching others his fighting skills. Although an attempt was made to get him to a hospital, he was unable to be revived. He was 78 years old. Blue Demon was buried wearing his trademark blue mask, which was never removed in public as he always kept his true identity a secret. ==Legacy== Blue Demon is considered one of the biggest legends of ''lucha libre'' second only to El Santo in terms of popularity and influence both in and outside of Mexico. The distinctive blue and silver mask of Blue Demon and Blue Demon Jr. is known worldwide and is an instantly recognizable symbol of Lucha Libre. On Wikipedia, The mask icon is used as part of some professional wrestling related tags and notices.{{efn|Displayed above is the Wikipedia Icon featuring Blue Demon's mask.}} On October 27, 2000, CMLL held their first ever ''[[Leyenda de Azul]]'' ("The Blue Legend") tournament in honor of Blue Demon.{{cite web | url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/emll/blue.html#2000 | title= Leyenda de Azul 2000 | date= October 27, 2000 | access-date= June 11, 2010 | publisher= ProWrestlingHistory.com}}{{cite news | author = Box y Lucha staff | title = 2000 Especial! | work = Box y Lucha Magazine | pages= 2–20 | id = issue 2488 | date = January 9, 2001 | language = es}} The winner of the tournament receives a championship belt that features Blue Demon as well as a plaque with a Blue Demon mask on it. The tournament has been held on a semi-regular basis ever since, The tournament was first endorsed by Blue Demon Jr., and later endorsed by Muñoz' son. Alfredo Muñoz, after Blue Demon Jr. stopped working for CMLL.From Copa In 2002, Blue Demon was ranked at 28 of the greatest professional wrestler of all time in the book ''The Top 100 Wrestlers of All Time'' by John Molinaro, edited by [[Dave Meltzer]] and [[Jeff Marek]].{{Cite book|last=Molinaro|first=John|year=2003|title=The Top 100 Wrestlers of All Time|publisher=Winding Stair Press |isbn=1-55366-305-5}} Starting in November 2015 [[Televisa]] and [[Sony Pictures Television]] began airing the first season of the [[Blue Demon (TV series)|Blue Demon]] [[television series]] featuring a fictionalized version of the early days of his career in the ring and personal life.{{cite web|title=Blue Demon es más que una simple historia de lucha libre|url=http://sipse.com/entretenimiento/blue-demon-serie-transmision-plataforma-blim-230992.html|website=sipse.com|date=November 18, 2016 |access-date=16 January 2017|language=es}}{{cite web|title=Aseguran que Televisa tiene que 'reciclar' locaciones por crisis (FOTOS)|url=http://mundohispanico.com/entretenimiento/aseguran-que-televisa-tiene-que-reciclar-locaciones-por-crisis-fotos|website=mundohispanico.com|access-date=16 January 2017|language=es|archive-date=December 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161218131514/http://mundohispanico.com/entretenimiento/aseguran-que-televisa-tiene-que-reciclar-locaciones-por-crisis-fotos|url-status=dead}} The third season of the series debuted on April 14, 2017, bringing the episode count to 65.{{cite web|title=¡Cada vez falta menos! Dr. X |image = Dick Beyer (cropped).jpg |caption = Beyer in 2010 |height = {{height|ft=5|in=10}} |weight = {{convert|265|lb|kg|abbr=on}} |birth_name = Richard John Beyer |birth_date = {{Birth date|1930|7|11|mf=y}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.f4wonline.com/content/view/13590/|title=Observer Radio, Interview with Dick Beyer, June 2, 2010|access-date=June 3, 2010|archive-date=June 6, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100606112729/http://www.f4wonline.com/content/view/13590|url-status=dead}} |birth_place = [[Buffalo, New York]], U.S. |death_date = {{death date and age|2019|3|7|1930|7|11|mf=y}} |death_place = [[Akron, New York]], U.S. |children = 4; Including [[Kurt Beyer|Kurt]] |education = [[Syracuse University]] |family = [[Billy Red Lyons]] (brother-in-law) |debut = December 29, 1954 |retired = July 29, 1993 }} '''Richard John Beyer''' (July 11, 1930 – March 7, 2019) was an American [[professional wrestler]] is best known by his ring names, '''The Destroyer''' and '''Doctor X'''. Among other places, he worked extensively in Japan and in 2017 he was awarded one of the country's highest honors, the [[Order of the Rising Sun]].{{Professional wrestling sidebar}} ==Early life== As an athlete at [[Syracuse University]], Beyer was a member of the [[varsity team|varsity]] [[American football|football]] and [[amateur wrestling|wrestling]] teams. He played in the 1953 [[Orange Bowl (game)|Orange Bowl]] for Syracuse.{{Cite web |title=Dick Beyer bio |url=https://www.onlineworldofwrestling.com/profile/dick-beyer/ |access-date=January 18, 2023 |publisher=Online World of Wrestling}} He graduated with a [[master's degree]] in [[education]] and was a member of the Fraternity of [[Phi Gamma Delta]]'s Syracuse Chapter, as well as an [[Eagle Scout (Boy Scouts of America)|Eagle Scout]] in the [[Boy Scouts of America]]. He was a schoolteacher and swim coach in New York until he began his wrestling career. Beyer worked the first seven years of his mat career near his Western New York home, due in large part to his coaching job and commitment to the U.S. Army Reserve.{{Cite web |last=Mooneyham |first=Mike |date=March 16, 2019 |title=Dick 'The Destroyer' Beyer: A lifetime of masks and memories |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/wrestling/dick-the-destroyer-beyer-a-lifetime-of-masks-and-memories/article_3e08fbbe-472c-11e9-a9ed-5b83005fbca8.html |access-date=May 28, 2021 |website=[[The Post and Courier]] |publisher=[[Evening Post Industries]] |language=en}} Beyer was a member of the wrestling team{{cite web |title=Syracuse University Wrestling Letterwinners |url=https://cuse.com/sports/2002/10/16/wrestlingletterwinners |website=[[Syracuse University Athletics]] |access-date=11 November 2024 |language=en}} and also served as an assistant to [[Ben Schwartzwalder]]. ==Professional wrestling career== [[File:Dr. X - Chicago Professional Wrestling - 26 April 1969 04.jpg|thumb|150px|Beyer in 1969 as Dr. X|left]] ===Worldwide Wrestling Associates (1954-1965)=== Beyer began as a babyface wrestler in the mid-1950s, and he was voted 1955 Rookie of the Year by the Wrestling Life magazine. His career as masked wrestler The Destroyer began in 1962 in [[Los Angeles, California|Los Angeles]]. Beyer traveled to California after [[Freddie Blassie]] praised Beyer's heel skills to local promoter [[John Bilbo (wrestler)|Jules Strongbow]], who informed him he would wrestle as the masked Destroyer. Beyer's original mask was hard to see through and itchy, but journeyman wrestler Ox Anderson lent him a mask fashioned from a woman's girdle, which served well for Beyer.{{Cite web |last=Mooneyham |first=Mike |date=January 7, 2012 |title=Destroyer unmasks secrets of success |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/staff/mike_mooneyham/destroyer-unmasks-secrets-of-success/article_97d1948b-6a47-5ffc-9802-c5118cd7bfad.html |access-date=June 2, 2021 |website=[[The Post and Courier]] |publisher=[[Evening Post Industries]] |language=en}} He boasted about his East Coast academic background to help develop his heel character. He used the [[Professional wrestling holds#Figure-four leglock|figure four]] leg lock (which became his signature finisher) on his way to the [[Worldwide Wrestling Associates]] (WWA) championship on July 27, 1962, in a win over [[Freddie Blassie]], who convinced him that the mask gimmick would give him a large push. He defended the championship for ten months. In June 1964, he returned to Los Angeles and beat [[Dick the Bruiser]] for another WWA championship run, losing it to [[Bob Ellis (wrestler)|Bob Ellis]] in September, regaining it in November, and finally dropping it in March 1965 to [[Pedro Morales]]. === Japan Pro Wrestling Alliance (1963–1971)=== In early 1963, Beyer wrestled three sold-out matches against [[Shohei Baba|Giant Baba]] at the [[Grand Olympic Auditorium|Olympic Auditorium]] in Los Angeles. In May 1963, he traveled to Japan for the first time in his career, to wrestle [[Rikidōzan]] in a match watched by over 70 million TV viewers, being Japan's highest rated show at the time.{{Cite web |date=February 11, 2018 |title=The Destroyer: A heel gets respect in Japan |url=https://www.tokyoreporter.com/japan-news/national/the-destroyer-a-heel-gets-respect-in-japan/ |access-date=May 28, 2021 |website= |publisher=[[Tokyo Reporter]]}} Beyer was also the last person to hold a victory over Rikidōzan before his death. Beyer was the first [[Wrestling mask|masked wrestler]] to compete in Japan regularly, and did regular tours for the [[Japan Pro Wrestling Alliance]] until 1971. In his last tour he made it to the semifinals of the annual World League tournament before losing to a rising [[Antonio Inoki]]. === American Wrestling Association (1966–1972) === Between 1966 and 1972, Beyer wrestled as Doctor X while in [[Minneapolis, Minnesota|Minneapolis]]. He had matches with many of the top names in the business including his real brother-in-law [[Billy Red Lyons]], who handed him his first [[American Wrestling Association]] (AWA) defeat on Minneapolis television, with a figure-four leglock. In August 1970, he took a chance at revenge against his former partner Blackjack Lanza. He stood in the center of the ring with announcer Marty O'Neill, who told the fans that Doctor X was a former coach from Syracuse University. Doctor X then removed his mask, handed it to promoter Eddie Williams, and wrestled the match as Dick Beyer. In other AWA cities, Beyer was unmasked by Lanza or Paul Diamond. In these matches, his name was said to be Bruce Marshall. He wanted to lose the mask because he and his family were set to go to Japan, where he would be The Destroyer again. During 1972, he had several battles with [[Ray Stevens (wrestler)|"Crippler" Ray Stevens]]. Their last match saw him written out of the AWA with a purported broken leg. === All Japan Pro Wrestling (1972–1993)=== From 1972 to 1979, Beyer wrestled in Japan on a deal with Giant Baba and [[Nippon Television|NTV]] of [[Tokyo]]. He feuded with [[Mil Máscaras]] in a series of seven matches, stating on his style, "He was the best competitor that I ever wrestled. He never gave you anything – it's true – but I didn't give him anything either. You talk about a [[Shoot wrestling|shoot]] or a half-shoot, and that's the kind of match that it was."{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=Greg |author-link=Greg Oliver |date=June 11, 2006 |title=Race & Hennig go over at Cauliflower Alley Club banquet |url=https://slamwrestling.net/index.php/2006/06/11/race-hennig-go-over-at-cauliflower-alley-club-banquet/ |access-date=May 28, 2021 |website=SLAM! Wrestling |publisher=[[Canadian Online Explorer]] |language=en-US}} He also helped promote [[All Japan Pro Wrestling]] (AJPW) for Baba and established himself as a [[gaijin tarento]] in a late-night TV show called ''Uwasa No Channel''.{{Cite web |date=February 13, 2018 |title=The Destroyer: World's greatest masked man |url=https://www.tokyoreporter.com/japan-news/national/the-destroyer-worlds-greatest-masked-man/ |access-date=May 28, 2021 |website= |publisher=[[Tokyo Reporter]] |language=en-US}} His appearance on the musical-comedy show only furthered the Destroyer's popularity in Japan, which led to him recording a Christmas album for his fans. He held the PWF United States Championship until 1979, when he left AJPW and the championship was abandoned. Beyer was also the first American wrestler signed to a Japanese promotion. His retirement match took place on July 29, 1993, where, he, his son [[Kurt Beyer]], and Giant Baba defeated [[Haruka Eigen]], [[Masanobu Fuchi]], and [[Masao Inoue (wrestler)|Masao Inoue]]. ==Later life and death== {{multiple image | width = | align = left | direction = vertical | footer = | image1 = Dick Beyer.jpg | caption1 = Beyer in June 2010. | image2 = Nighthawk with Destroyer and Mil Mascaras.jpg | caption2 = Beyer (left) with [[Mil Máscaras]] and Nighthawk. }} Beyer went into semi-retirement in [[Akron, New York]], in 1984. Until 1995, he taught [[physical education]] in the Akron Central School District, and coached football, wrestling and swimming.{{Cite magazine |last=Klavon |first=Ken |date=February 11, 2020 |title=Japan's Park Golf finds first home in America |url=https://www.si.com/golf/travel/feature-2020-02-11-japans-park-golf-finds-home-in-america |access-date=January 18, 2023 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |language=en}} He served on the board of directors of the [[Cauliflower Alley Club]], which holds annual reunions in Las Vegas. He was a member of [[Toastmasters International]], a public speaking club, and carried the club designation of Certified Toastmaster. He inducted [[Gorgeous George]] into the [[WWE Hall of Fame]] on March 27, 2010. On August 27, 2011, Beyer, along with his son, returned to Japan to take part in [[All Together (professional wrestling)|All Together]], a charity event copromoted by AJPW, [[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]] and [[Pro Wrestling Noah]]. Appearing under his Destroyer mask, he hosted the Destroyer Cup and presented a trophy to its winner, [[Kentaro Shiga]].{{cite web|url=http://www.njpw.co.jp/match/detail_result_game.php?e=276&c=3266|title=東日本大震災復興支援チャリティープロレス ''All Together''|access-date=2013-09-10|work=[[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]]|language=ja}} In 2013, he opened Destroyer Park Golf in Akron, the first [[park golf]] course in the United States. On November 4, 2017, the Japanese government awarded Beyer the [[Order of the Rising Sun]], Gold and Silver Rays, for "a lifetime spent promoting goodwill and bi-cultural exchanges between Japan and the United States".{{Cite web |date=February 4, 2018 |title=Ex-pro wrestling star The Destroyer receives the Order of the Rising Sun |url=https://www.tokyoreporter.com/japan-news/breaking/pro-wrestling-star-the-destroyer-receives-the-order-of-the-rising-sun/ |access-date=January 18, 2023 |publisher=[[Tokyo Reporter]]}} Beyer died in his bed at his home in Akron on March 7, 2019, at the age of 88, surrounded by his wife and all of his children. He had been suffering from health issues and spent time in hospice care.{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Steven |date=March 7, 2019 |title=The Destroyer Dick Beyer dies |url=http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Wrestling/2019/03/07/22793823.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190308024923/http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Wrestling/2019/03/07/22793823.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 8, 2019 |access-date=January 18, 2023 |website=SLAM!
