==Promotion and reception== Cassidy was first unveiled as a playable character at the [[PAX East]] convention in June 2015.{{cite web |website=[[PC Gamer]] |title=Hands-on with Overwatch's two new characters |date=March 6, 2015 |last=Lahti |first=Evan |accessdate=June 3, 2023 |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/overwatch-new-characters-pax-east-2015/ |archive-date=June 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190605100650/https://www.pcgamer.com/overwatch-new-characters-pax-east-2015/ |url-status=live }} To promote ''Overwatch'' and the character, Blizzard Entertainment released a cosplay guide and promotional images themed around holidays.{{cite book|last=Burns|first=Matt|editor-last1=Simpson|editor-first1=Robert|editor-last2=Gary|editor-first2=Cate|editor-last3=Monahan|editor-first3=Allison|title=The Art of Overwatch Limited Edition|publisher=[[Dark Horse Comics]]|date=October 24, 2017|isbn=9781506705538 |pages=360–361}} Joseph Knoop of ''[[The Daily Dot]]'' felt the character's personality was the most significant factor for his appeal, noting that while he felt the character's gameplay was lacking there was "no getting around the fact that a cowboy with 'BAMF' on his belt buckle and a robotic arm is totally awesome".{{cite web|last=Knoop|first=Joseph|url=https://www.dailydot.com/parsec/best-overwatch-character/|title=Every Overwatch character, ranked|work=[[The Daily Dot]]|date=May 21, 2021|access-date=November 7, 2023|archive-date=April 19, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190419045956/https://www.dailydot.com/parsec/best-overwatch-character/|url-status=live}} Author Matt Margini cited Cassidy as an example of the enduring nature of the cowboy aesthetic, stating that ''Overwatch'' wouldn't be the same without the "(literal) straight shooter who keeps the game tethered both thematically and mechanically to more grounded forms of gunplay.{{cite book |first=Matt |last=Margini |title=Red Dead Redemption |date=May 2020 |publisher=Boss Fight Books |isbn=9781940535241 |chapter=Cowboy}} Cass Marshall of ''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]'' stated that while Cassidy was "a silly character", it was part of his charm, and in some ways represents the best parts of the franchise's setting. They additionally praised the character's sense of decency, putting others before himself or the mission to keep them safe and his interactions that contrasted against the more stern faces of the Overwatch group. Marshall hoped to see more of the character, stating that despite Cassidy's flaws "he still manages to be one of ''Overwatch''{{'}}s best heroes, and that's something we can all admire."{{cite web|accessdate=November 7, 2023|date=October 17, 2018|first=Cass|last=Marshall|title=McCree's Wild West sensibilities make him Overwatch's best hero|url=https://www.heroesneverdie.com/2018/10/17/17984594/overwatch-mccree-best-hero-character-lore|website=[[Polygon (website)|Heroes Never Die]]|archive-date=November 12, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231112070420/https://www.heroesneverdie.com/2018/10/17/17984594/overwatch-mccree-best-hero-character-lore|url-status=live}} ''[[Kill Screen]]''{{'}}s Chris Priestman felt Cassidy embodied the "falsity" of how old west gunslingers were perceived, drawing direct inspiration from [[Val Kilmer]]'s portrayal of [[Doc Holliday]] and [[Clint Eastwood]]'s [[The Man with No Name]] and adding that while visually Cassidy was a joke, "as cheesy as his belt buckle is [...] it's not without merit." Priestman further stated that while the character felt out of place in the ''Overwatch'' cast, and his own initial assumption was to assume Cassidy was an "asshole", the character inspired imagery of popular depictions of cowboys and the old [[Wild West]], as opposed to simply being someone in a costume "trying to hide behind the image". He shared Marshall's approval of his sense of decency, and added that Cassidy "has it where it counts [...] You're supposed to feel intimidated by the stone-cold manliness he resurrects from the past."{{cite web |first=Chris |last=Priestman |accessdate=November 7, 2023 |website=[[Kill Screen]] |title=Who you kidding? McCree is Overwatch's true shooter |date=August 12, 2016 |url=https://killscreen.com/previously/articles/mccree/ |archive-date=November 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231106074543/https://killscreen.com/previously/articles/mccree/ |url-status=live }} In May 2017, the [[Social networking service|social networking]] website [[Tumblr]] sifted through its data in order to determine which character pairings in ''Overwatch'' were the most popular. '''Astarion Ancunín''' is a fictional character from [[Larian Studios]]' ''[[Baldur's Gate]]'' video game series, which is based on the tabletop [[fantasy]] role-playing system of ''[[Dungeons & Dragons]]'' and set in the [[Forgotten Realms]]. Making his first appearance in 2023's ''[[Baldur's Gate 3]]'', Astarion can serve as the game's primary protagonist or as a recruitable [[Party (role playing games)|party member]]. He is a [[Rogue (Dungeons & Dragons)|rogue]], specializing in stealth, lockpicking, and sneak attacks. In the game, Astarion is kidnapped alongside several other party members and infected with an [[Illithid]] parasite and must search for a way to cure himself. Early in the story, he is revealed to be a [[Vampire Spawn|vampire spawn]], and his personal quest focuses on evading and hunting down his former master, Cazador Szarr.

When Astarion was initially encountered during ''Baldur's Gate 3'''s [[early access]] period, he quickly became a fan-favorite. His prominence on the game's box art and his major role in subsequent trailers and marketing made this evident. He also earned critical praise for his [[Deadpan|dry]], sassy [[characterization]], intriguing [[backstory]], and [[sex appeal]]. Astarion is voiced and performed by the English actor [[Neil Newbon]], who has also received praise, winning several awards for his performance, including the 2023 [[Golden Joystick Awards|Golden Joystick Award]] for Best Supporting Performer, and Best Performance at the [[2023 Game Awards]].

==Creation and development==
[[File:Neil Newbon by Gage Skidmore.jpg|left|thumb|[[Neil Newbon]], who provided the voice and motion capture for Astarion, received critical acclaim and several awards for his performance.|alt=Newbon in 2024]]
Astarion was created by and primarily written by ''[[Baldur's Gate 3]]'' senior writer Stephen Rooney, and is voiced and [[Motion capture|motion captured]] by English actor [[Neil Newbon]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=The voice of Baldur's Gate 3's Astarion talks TTRPGs, storytelling, and the {{as written|glamo|urous [sic]}} 'fury and the wrath' of playing vampires|last=Randall|first=Harvey|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=August 14, 2023|access-date=January 29, 2024|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-voice-of-baldurs-gate-3s-astarion-talks-ttrpgs-storytelling-and-the-glamourous-fury-and-the-wrath-of-playing-vampires/|language=en|archive-date=January 29, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240129170619/https://www.pcgamer.com/the-voice-of-baldurs-gate-3s-astarion-talks-ttrpgs-storytelling-and-the-glamourous-fury-and-the-wrath-of-playing-vampires/|url-status=live}}</ref> Discussing his process for bringing the character to life, Newbon stated that he was heavily influenced by [[Commedia dell'arte|commedia dell’arte]], a comedic style of Italian theatre, and their inclusion of an amoral jester known as [[Arlecchino]]. Astarion's mannerisms were adapted from several of Newbon's friends and by several creative individuals, namely makeup artist Leendert Van Nimwegen, actor Giles Foreman, and cabaret performer [[Reuben Kaye]]. Newbon stated that he developed some of the vampiric aspects of Astarion's character from a local stray cat, explaining that "the way the cat moves, or the way the cat looks at you. The way the cat will allow you to come closer and then rip your hand off when it's bored 'cause that's enough. 'That's enough, now. No touching now, darling.'"<ref>{{Cite web|title=Baldur's Gate 3's Astarion Reveals the Inspiration for His Character [Exclusive]|last=Cripe|first=Michael|work=[[The Escapist (magazine)|The Escapist]]|date=October 17, 2023|access-date=December 28, 2023|url=https://www.escapistmagazine.com/baldurs-gate-3s-astarion-reveals-the-inspiration-for-his-character-exclusive/|language=en|archive-date=December 29, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229001540/https://www.escapistmagazine.com/baldurs-gate-3s-astarion-reveals-the-inspiration-for-his-character-exclusive/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Newbon acknowledged the importance of the character and the exploration of abuse through his questline, stating that "People have come up to me and said that they've felt inspired to deal with their own trauma. As a survivor myself, I understand when they talk to me about it - what they mean. That they feel seen by the game, they feel understood by the characters. That is a testament to this amazing, beautiful masterpiece that [[Larian Studios|Larian]], [[Swen Vincke|Swen]], the writing team have all put together and created."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Baldur's Gate 3's Astarion actor was "very close to quitting" acting before landing a role in the RPG|last=Bellingham|first=Hope|work=[[GamesRadar+]]|date=November 13, 2023|access-date=December 29, 2023|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/baldurs-gate-3s-astarion-actor-was-very-close-to-quitting-acting-before-landing-a-role-in-the-rpg//|language=en|archive-date=December 29, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229005525/https://www.gamesradar.com/baldurs-gate-3s-astarion-actor-was-very-close-to-quitting-acting-before-landing-a-role-in-the-rpg//|url-status=live}}</ref> He also mentioned, in reference to being a [[method actor]], that he forced himself to only use memories that were at least seven years old, as is a guideline for that school of acting.<ref name="Randall"/>

Discussing what it was like to play Astarion, Newbon explained that he was given creative freedom with some heavy themes. He found it very fascinating to play a character who initially appears as a "decadent, manipulative, hedonistic vampire", but is actually deeply traumatised and wears a façade to protect himself from the pain and will do anything to keep his newfound freedom. He also praised the character's [[pansexuality]], and discussed how an [[intimacy coordinator]] was available for all of the performers to help them bring the game's sex scenes to life.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Neil Newbon On Becoming Astarion In Baldur's Gate 3|last=King|first=Jade|work=The Gamer|date=November 1, 2023|access-date=December 29, 2023|url=https://www.thegamer.com/neil-newbon-interview-astarion-baldurs-gate-3/|language=en|archive-date=December 20, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231220061834/https://www.thegamer.com/neil-newbon-interview-astarion-baldurs-gate-3/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Portraying the struggles of Astarion as a survivor of trauma and abuse was a difficult balance for Newbon, who admitted that "there [was] a lot of stuff that came very close to home" and that he had to take care to separate the aspects of his own life that he was bringing to the character to the truth of the actual character in the script, and reflected upon the care he and the developers took with his storyline, explaining "it's not a gimmick. He's not [traumatised] because it's 'just another idea for a character story' …  this was a very fleshed out, deep, layered observation of a character in trouble and jeopardy, having gone through trauma—and then what they do to get out of that, and what they can do with their newfound sense of freedom, and what that means to them."<ref name="Randall">{{Cite web|title=Baldur's Gate 3's Astarion, Neil Newbon, on acting the truth of trauma as a survivor: 'There's a lot of stuff that came very close to home'|last=Randall|first=Harvey|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=August 17, 2023|access-date=December 28, 2023|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/baldurs-gate-3s-astarion-neil-newbon-on-acting-the-truth-of-trauma-as-a-survivor-theres-a-lot-of-stuff-that-came-very-close-to-home/|language=en|archive-date=December 29, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229004747/https://www.pcgamer.com/baldurs-gate-3s-astarion-neil-newbon-on-acting-the-truth-of-trauma-as-a-survivor-theres-a-lot-of-stuff-that-came-very-close-to-home/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In developing Astarion's personality, Newbon said, "He was probably quite decadent in the past, perhaps abusing his power a little bit. I see him as being very intelligent — very erudite — and highly manipulative when he wants to be. Very vulnerable and traumatized, but also incredibly witty and funny. He's got etiquette, he's articulate, and he's very sophisticated. He's a lover of the arts without, I believe, having the talent to produce art himself. He's also rather good-looking, and he's not afraid to use that as a way to shield himself or to get what he wants. He's ''immoral'', not amoral. I would say he's quite aware of morality. He just ''chooses'' not to [be moral], darling, you know?" When asked about how Astarion sees himself, Newbon continued, "I know how ''I'' see him. In the script, he does see himself in certain ways, but he's always very, very guarded about it. He's always careful not to give too much away because if he does that, then he starts losing power and can theoretically be manipulated. So, it's a very interesting situation for him to regard himself openly like that."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hoops |first=Jessica |date=2023-10-17 |title=BG3: Neil Newbon Talks Astarion Being More Than a Pretty Face |url=https://www.escapistmagazine.com/baldurs-gate-3-bg-3-astarion-pretty-face-interview/ |access-date=2024-03-14 |website=The Escapist |language=en-US}}</ref>

When asked how Astarion evolved over the course of shooting the game, Neil said, "I used a lot of tools to really explore the character under his circumstances. The needs and wants [were] very clear. To be free is super objective, but that's his ultimate aim, to be free, whatever the cost. That also helped me with the background that [the writers] gave me; he was a magistrate, he's a High Elf, he's of noble class. He's a Baldurian, and he's decadent, he's hedonistic, and he had this amazing life before being turned into a vampire. All of that feeds into the background work and it helps me create habits [for the character]."<ref>{{Citation |title=🔴Astarion Actor Neil Newbon talks BALDUR'S GATE 3, Bear Romance & Why this role gets him Emotional | date=8 August 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ikUV7hletb0 |access-date=2024-03-14 |language=en}}</ref>

Stephen Rooney, writer of Astarion, was asked about where the idea for the character came from and responded, "It very quickly became clear what was at the core of [Astarion's] story. We have a vampire who is a [[Vampire spawn|vampire ''spawn'']], which we had to do because [he couldn't be] an ''actual'' [[Vampire (Dungeons & Dragons)|vampire]]; [they're] ''very'' powerful creatures in [[Dungeons & Dragons|Dungeons and Dragons]]. So, we had to make him a vampire spawn, which means he would have to have a master, which means that he would have to be ''removed'' from his master. So, you end up in this situation where this character is, in theory, very powerful, and is chasing that power and that freedom, but is also incredibly weak and incredibly vulnerable. Playing off of that dichotomy between a hunger for power and a very real vulnerability." Rooney continued with, "We hit on what was cool and interesting and what was at the emotional core of that character very early on. We knew very early on where [Astarion's] starting point was, and it was fairly clear what his end point was going to be."<ref>{{Citation |title=Astarion's Origin: Baldur's Gate 3 Writer Stephen Rooney Reveals All in an Exclusive Interview! | date=23 September 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W9Mlr5UbiyQ |access-date=2024-03-14 |language=en}}</ref>

When asked about the main characteristics that had to be represented [in Astarion], Rooney said the following: "When you meet Astarion in the game, the first thing he does is pull a knife on you. He has a certain appreciation for violence, I guess. I think it's important to have that, but he's a vampire, he's all about those darker sides of humanity. But at the same time, he's really fun! It was important to me that that is also represented. Those are the two sides [to him], he's gonna stab you, but will he have a smile on his face as he does it? I don't know, that's kind of him in a nutshell."<ref>{{Citation |title=Stephen Rooney {{!}} Idle Insights {{!}} Idle Champions {{!}} D&D | date=11 September 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C6HTEsnKb7E |access-date=2024-03-14 |language=en}}</ref>

===Gameplay===
As a [[Rogue (Dungeons & Dragons)|rogue]], Astarion wears light armor and is proficient with several bladed weapons, including daggers, rapiers and longswords, as well as longbows and crossbows. Astarion is skilled in acrobatics, deception, perception, performance, persuasion, sleight of hand, and stealth, making him well-suited to several tasks, including picking locks and disarming traps, which are invaluable early on in the game if the player has not also created a rogue character. As a [[Elf (Dungeons & Dragons)|High Elf]], he naturally has the ability to cast a Fire Bolt but does not have any other magical abilities, unless the player selects specific character options. As a vampire spawn, Astarion has a unique Vampire Bite ability which drains an enemy of some of their health and transfers it to Astarion, though this ability is not unlocked until the player finds out that Astarion is a vampire during the story. Depending on the outcome of his personal quest, he may gain an upgraded version of this ability, known as Ascendant Bite, and the power to transform into a cloud of mist.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Astarion Companion Guide|work=[[IGN]]|date=September 4, 2023|access-date=January 29, 2024|url=https://www.ign.com/wikis/baldurs-gate-3/Astarion_Companion_Guide|language=en|archive-date=January 29, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240129170619/https://www.ign.com/wikis/baldurs-gate-3/Astarion_Companion_Guide|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Appearances==
===''Baldur's Gate 3''===
{{see also|Baldur's Gate 3#Plot}}
Astarion is a [[Elf (Dungeons & Dragons)|High Elf]] [[Rogue (Dungeons & Dragons)|rogue]] who is also a [[vampire spawn]] first introduced in ''[[Baldur's Gate 3]]''. He was kidnapped by [[illithid]]s and infected with a parasite. Players can choose to play Astarion as an origin character or he can be recruited in the party as a companion.<ref name="GameRant">{{Cite web|title=Baldur's Gate 3: Why Astarion is One of the Best Companions|last=Mitchell Jewett|first=Katelyn|work=[[GameRant]]|date=September 5, 2023|access-date=January 29, 2024|url=https://gamerant.com/baldurs-gate-3-astarion-best-companion-rogue-romance-mindflayer-good-why/|language=en|archive-date=November 27, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231127094617/https://gamerant.com/baldurs-gate-3-astarion-best-companion-rogue-romance-mindflayer-good-why/|url-status=live}}</ref> As an adventuring companion, Astarion will often offer commentary on events. As part of the game's companion approval system, Astarion will generally approve of displays of power or mockery. Additionally, he approves choices that support autonomy, and helping certain characters. Astarion will disapprove of displays of weakness and certain acts of kindness that offer no reward. He also resents players who attempt to control or restrict him in some way.

Players can learn more about Astarion and influence his development through his companion quest, "The Pale Elf". This quest reveals Astarion is a vampire spawn. The player makes a deal with Astarion over whether he is allowed to feed on their enemies or must stick to non-intelligent creatures. Throughout the game, Astarion can reveal more about past, such as information about his master, Cazador Szarr, who tormented him and his six vampire siblings for two hundred years. He expresses joy that his capture has freed him from Cazador, and that the parasite has eliminated his weakness to sunlight. If the player enters into a romance with Astarion or has high approval with him, they will learn about the strange scars that Cazador had carved into his back, though he does not know what they mean. During the adventure, it is possible for Astarion to make a deal with the devil Raphael to decipher the meaning of his scars, where he reveals they are part of a seven part contract with the archdevil Mephistopheles.

During the game's third act, the party can come across two of Cazador's spawn, who reveal preparations for a ritual known as the Black Mass are underway. Several of Astarion's fellow spawn can attempt to kidnap him; if successful, he will be tortured at Cazador's mansion until rescued. If not captured, Astarion and the rest of the party can infiltrate the mansion themselves, and find that the Black Mass has already begun. Upon gaining entry to Cazador's study, Astarion is shocked to discover an entire underground dungeon that holds thousands of imprisoned vampire spawn. Astarion is horrified, believing that the people he and his siblings had been sent to hunt were long dead. The party eventually confronts Cazador, who reveals that the scars on the backs of his seven original spawn will be used to sacrifice them and the other prisoners, allowing him to gain enough power to ascend.

Once Cazador is defeated, the player is then tasked with influencing how Astarion's story ends. If they support Astarion completing the Black Mass ritual himself, Cazador, his vampire siblings, and the seven thousand prisoners will be sacrificed and Astarion will become a vampire ascendant. Astarion's personality will significantly change if he ascends, becoming more arrogant and controlling. Astarion will request that a player he is in a relationship with became his spawn and he will break up with them if they refuse. If he does not complete the ritual, Astarion kills Cazador. The player then may choose to advise Astarion over whether to release the prisoners, kill them, or leave them in the cells. Following the completion of his quest, an Astarion who did not ascend will take romanced players to visit his grave, and will confess his love.

Following the game's final battle, if Astarion is a vampire spawn, he will become vulnerable to sunlight again. If the player is in a relationship with Astarion, they can pledge to help him find a permanent cure. His behaviour during the epilogue is dependent on the choice made during his companion quest: if the ritual was completed, although Astarion will continue to retain his arrogant persona, he will be proud to have the player side by side with him. If Astarion remained a spawn, he continues to act sarcastically and flamboyantly, bragging about his time as an adventurer and exhibiting a renewed sense of self that is accepting of his own identity and nature.

===Novels and comic books===

In April 2026, [[Penguin Random House]] announced the prequel novel ''Baldur's Gate 3: Astarion'' by [[T. Kingfisher]]. It released on September 29, 2026; ''Baldur's Gate 3'' senior writer Stephen Rooney was a consultant on the novel. The audiobook edition was narrated by Astarion's voice actor Neil Newbon.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Glennon |first=Jen |date=April 24, 2026 |title=Exclusive: Baldur's Gate 3 is officially getting a prequel novel starring Astarion |url=https://www.polygon.com/bg3-baldurs-gate-3-astarion-prequel-novel-release-date/ |access-date=July 24, 2026 |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Yin-Poole |first=Wesley |date=April 27, 2026 |title=Astarion Is Getting a Prequel Novel Set During His Time in Servitude to the Vampire Lord Cazador Szarr in the Years Leading Up to the Events of Baldur's Gate 3 |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/astarion-is-getting-a-prequel-novel-set-during-his-time-in-servitude-to-the-vampire-lord-cazador-szarr-in-the-years-leading-up-to-the-events-of-baldurs-gate-3 |access-date=July 24, 2026 |website=[[IGN]] |language=en}}</ref> The prequel is a [[tragedy]]; it splits time between Astarion's childhood and an adventure after he became one of Cazador's spawn. Kingfisher explained that Astarion "to a certain extent" has some personal growth in the prequel novel, however, the character could not change much as Astarion's "big arc in the game is reclaiming his agency". She commented that "I think that one of the things about tragedies is that the ending is inevitable and you can see it coming. You know he's not going to find true love and it's going to go to hell".<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |last=Codega |first=Lin |date=September 23, 2026 |title=T. Kingfisher’s Astarion is hilarious, heartbreaking, and utterly tragic |url=https://www.rascal.news/t-kingfishers-astarion-is-hilarious-heartbreaking-and-utterly-tragic/ |access-date=October 18, 2026 |website=Rascal News |language=en}}</ref> Lin Codega of ''Rascal'' wrote that "Kingfisher couldn't give him what he wanted, she couldn't fix him, and she could only encourage a bit of character growth. She thinks of the book as missing its third act – which is, of course, where ''Baldur's Gate 3'' steps in to finish the character growth that this book begins to explore".<ref name="Website-1" />

In October 2026, [[Dark Horse Comics]] announced that the first arc of the upcoming [[Ongoing series|ongoing comic series]] ''Baldur's Gate III'' will focus on Astarion. This six-issue arc will be written by [[Alyssa Wong]], with art by Vincenzo Carratù.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alverson |first=Brigid |date=October 16, 2026 |title=NYCC: Dark Horse Plans Longer Series for Licensed Properties |url=https://icv2.com/articles/news/view/63648/nycc-dark-horse-plans-longer-series-licensed-properties |access-date=October 18, 2026 |website=[[ICv2]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite press release |title=Dark Horse Comics Announces Ongoing Baldur's Gate 3 Comic Series at NYCC |date=October 9, 2026 |publisher=Dark Horse Comics |url=https://www.darkhorse.com/newsfeed/alyssa-wong-and-vincenzo-carrat%C3%B9-reunite-for-a-tale-of-murder-and-mayhem-in-the-new-ongoing-series-baldurs-gate-3/ |access-date=October 18, 2026}}</ref>

===Other games===
Astarion was added as a champion to the incremental game ''[[Idle Champions of the Forgotten Realms]]'' in September 2023.<ref>{{Cite press release |author=<!-- not stated --> |title=Idle Champion Spotlight: Astarion |date=September 1, 2023 |publisher=Codename Entertainment Inc. |url=https://codenameentertainment.com/?page=idle_champions&post_id=1565 |access-date=October 19, 2026}}</ref>

Outside of video games, the character was included on cards for ''[[Magic: the Gathering]]''{{'}}s "Commander Legends: The Battle For Baldur's Gate" set, appearing on both a regular and a special "showcase" card.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/card-image-gallery/commander-legends-battle-for-baldurs-gate-variants |date=2022-05-25 |access-date=2023-12-23 |title=Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate Variant Card Image Gallery |website=[[Wizards of the Coast]] |archive-date=2023-12-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231223192747/https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/card-image-gallery/commander-legends-battle-for-baldurs-gate-variants |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Astarion's Book of Hungers'' (2025), a digital [[Sourcebook (gaming)|sourcebook]] for the [[Editions of Dungeons & Dragons|5th edition]] of ''[[Dungeons & Dragons]]'', included [[marginalia]] by the titular character. It also included lore about Astarion from before the events of ''Baldur's Gate 3''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Russell |first=Mollie |date=August 4, 2025 |title=DnD's going all in on fanservice, and I'm nervous for the Forgotten Realms books |url=https://www.wargamer.com/dnd/forgotten-realms-fanservice |access-date=October 19, 2026 |website=[[Wargamer (website)|Wargamer]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jewett |first=Katelyn Mitchell |date=November 11, 2025 |title=Everything Astarion's Book of Hungers Reveals About Baldur's Gate 3's Astarion |url=https://gamerant.com/baldurs-gate-3-dungeons-dragons-astarion-book-of-hungers/ |access-date=October 19, 2026 |website=GameRant |language=en}}</ref>

==Critical reception==
When ''Baldur's Gate 3'' was released, Astarion instantly became a fan-favorite character, with [[NBC News]] and [[CNN]] reporting that videos featuring him had received over half a billion views on [[TikTok]], with fans citing his heartthrob features, sassy quips and enjoyable romance arc as some of their primary reasons for their enjoyment of the character. Additionally, other players stated that they identified with his story as a survivor of trauma and abuse, and considered him a comfort character for those with similar experiences. Discussing reaction to the character, [[Neil Newbon]], Astarion's voice actor, noted "it is incredibly touching to have people come up to me and say, 'Astarion's story made me feel seen,' and that I Either way, Astarion is funny, extremely flirtatious, and the right amount of trouble to get any D&D player interested."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Best Baldur's Gate 3 Companions tier list: Astarion, Shadowheart, Halsin & more|last=Fillby|first=Jessica|work=Dexerto|date=December 22, 2023|access-date=December 28, 2023|url=https://www.dexerto.com/baldurs-gate/best-baldurs-gate-3-companions-tier-list-astarion-shadowheart-halsin-more-2241514/|language=en|archive-date=December 29, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229000357/https://www.dexerto.com/baldurs-gate/best-baldurs-gate-3-companions-tier-list-astarion-shadowheart-halsin-more-2241514/|url-status=live}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Den of Geek]]'', Matthew Byrd ranked Astarion as the game's fourth best companion, explaining that "Astarion's story is not only compelling, but it's one of the few companion stories that are interesting right out of the gate rather than after you've invested considerable time into getting to know a character. Astarion's story is never quite what you think it's going to be, and I mean that in the best way possible."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Best Baldur's Gate 3 Companions: Every Companion Ranked Worst to Best|last=Bryd|first=Matthew|work=[[Den of Geek]]|date=August 18, 2023|access-date=December 28, 2023|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/games/baldurs-gate-3-best-companions-ranked/|language=en|archive-date=December 22, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231222191431/https://www.denofgeek.com/games/baldurs-gate-3-best-companions-ranked/|url-status=live}}</ref> Katelyn Mitchell Jewett of ''[[Game Rant]]'' declared Astarion one of the game's best companions, citing his complex and compelling story, his usefulness as a party member, his romance plotline, and his unique take on the central conflict.”<ref name="GameRant"/> Writing for the same publication, Carrie Talbot praised the characterization of Astarion, and the writing and performance of Rooney and Newbon, for revolutionizing the morality system in roleplaying games.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Baldur's Gate 3 knocked my RPG halo off, and it's all Astarion's fault|last=Talbot|first=Carrie|work=[[GamesRadar+]]|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=December 28, 2023|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/baldurs-gate-3-knocked-my-rpg-halo-off-and-its-all-astarions-fault/|language=en|archive-date=December 29, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229002426/https://www.gamesradar.com/baldurs-gate-3-knocked-my-rpg-halo-off-and-its-all-astarions-fault/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2024, a poll conducted by [[British Academy of Film and Television Arts|BAFTA]] with around 4,000 respondents named Astarion as the seventeenth most iconic video-game character of all time.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Lara Croft Crowned Most Iconic Video Games Character of All Time, According to BAFTA Poll |url=https://www.bafta.org/media-centre/press-releases/bafta-most-iconic-character-poll-results |work=BAFTA |date=2024-04-04 }}</ref>
